verses.1:1: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
verses.1:2: Now the earth was unformed and empty, and darkness lay over the face of the deep; and the Spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters.
verses.1:3: And God said, "Let there be light"; and light came to be.
verses.1:4: And God saw the light, that it was good; and God divided between the light and the darkness.
verses.1:5: And God named the light Day, and the darkness He named Night. And evening came to be, and morning came to be: one day.
verses.1:6: Then God said, "Let a firmament come to be in the midst of the waters, and let it divide between waters and waters."
verses.1:7: So God made the firmament, and divided the waters which were beneath the firmament from the waters which were above the firmament; and so it came to be.
verses.1:8: And God named the firmament Heavens. And evening came to be, and morning came to be: a second day.
verses.1:9: Then God said, "Let the waters beneath the heavens be gathered together into one place, and let the dry ground appear"; and so it came to be.
verses.1:10: And God named the dry ground Earth, and the gathering together of the waters He named Seas; and God saw that it was good.
verses.1:11: Then God said, "Let the earth sprout forth tender vegetation: seed-bearing herbs, and fruit trees yielding fruit according to their kind, whose seed is in itself upon the earth"; and so it came to be.
verses.1:12: So the earth brought forth tender vegetation, herbs yielding seed according to their kind, and trees yielding fruit whose seed is in itself according to their kind; and God saw that it was good.
verses.1:13: And evening came to be, and morning came to be: a third day.
verses.1:14: Then God said, "Let luminaries come to be in the firmament of the heavens to divide between the day and the night; and let them serve for signs, and for appointed seasons, and for days and years;
verses.1:15: and let them be for luminaries in the firmament of the heavens to shed light upon the earth"; and so it came to be.
verses.1:16: So God made the two great luminaries: the greater luminary to hold dominion over the day, and the lesser luminary to hold dominion over the night, and the stars also.
verses.1:17: And God set them in the firmament of the heavens to shed light upon the earth,
verses.1:18: and to hold dominion over the day and over the night, and to divide between the light and the darkness; and God saw that it was good.
verses.1:19: And evening came to be, and morning came to be: a fourth day.
verses.1:20: Then God said, "Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures, and let winged fowl fly above the earth across the face of the firmament of the heavens."
verses.1:21: So God created the great sea monsters, and every living creature that moves, with which the waters swarmed according to their kind, and every winged bird according to its kind; and God saw that it was good.
verses.1:22: And God blessed them, saying, "Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas; and let the fowl multiply in the earth."
verses.1:23: And evening came to be, and morning came to be: a fifth day.
verses.1:24: Then God said, "Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kind: livestock, and creeping things, and beasts of the earth according to their kind"; and so it came to be.
verses.1:25: So God made the beasts of the earth according to their kind, and the livestock according to their kind, and every creeping thing of the ground according to its kind; and God saw that it was good.
verses.1:26: Then God said, "Let Us make man in Our image, according to Our likeness; and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the heavens, and over the livestock, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth."
verses.1:27: And God created the man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them.
verses.1:28: And God blessed them, and God said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth, and subdue it; and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the heavens, and over every living creature that moves upon the earth."
verses.1:29: And God said, "Behold, I have given to you every seed-bearing herb which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree in which is the fruit of a seed-bearing tree; to you it shall be for food.
verses.1:30: And to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the heavens, and to everything that creeps upon the earth in which is a living soul, I have given every green herb for food"; and so it came to be.
verses.1:31: And God beheld everything which He had made, and behold, it was exceedingly good. And evening came to be, and morning came to be: the sixth day.
verses.2:1: Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them.
verses.2:2: And by the seventh day God had completed His work which He had made; and He rested on the seventh day from all His work which He had made.
verses.2:3: And God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on it He rested from all His work which God had created to make.
verses.2:4: These are the generations of the heavens and of the earth when they were created, in the day that the LORD God made earth and heavens.
verses.2:5: Now no shrub of the field was yet in the earth, and no herb of the field had yet sprung up, for the LORD God had not caused it to rain upon the earth, and there was no man to till the ground;
verses.2:6: but a mist rose up from the earth and watered the whole face of the ground.
verses.2:7: Then the LORD God fashioned man of dust from the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
verses.2:8: And the LORD God planted a garden in Eden toward the east, and there He placed the man whom He had fashioned.
verses.2:9: And out of the ground the LORD God caused to spring up every tree pleasant to the sight and good for food, and the tree of life in the midst of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
verses.2:10: Now a river flowed forth from Eden to water the garden, and from there it divided and became four headwaters.
verses.2:11: The name of the first is Pishon; it is the one that winds around all the land of Havilah, where the gold is.
verses.2:12: And the gold of that land is good; bdellium and the onyx stone are there.
verses.2:13: And the name of the second river is Gihon; it is the one that winds around all the land of Cush.
verses.2:14: And the name of the third river is Tigris; it is the one that flows east of Assyria. And the fourth river is Euphrates.
verses.2:15: So the LORD God took the man and settled him in the garden of Eden to till it and to keep it.
verses.2:16: And the LORD God laid a command upon the man, saying, "Of every tree of the garden you may freely eat;
verses.2:17: yet of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat, for in the day that you eat of it you shall surely die."
verses.2:18: And the LORD God said, "It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make for him a helper corresponding to him."
verses.2:19: Now out of the ground the LORD God had formed every beast of the field and every fowl of the heavens, and He brought them to the man to see what he would call them; and whatever the man called each living creature, that was its name.
verses.2:20: So the man gave names to all livestock, and to the fowl of the heavens, and to every beast of the field; yet for man there was not found a helper corresponding to him.
verses.2:21: Then the LORD God caused a deep slumber to fall upon the man, and he slept; and He took one of his ribs, and closed up flesh in its place.
verses.2:22: And the rib which the LORD God had taken from the man He built into a woman, and brought her to the man.
verses.2:23: And the man said, "This at last is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called Woman, for out of Man was she taken."
verses.2:24: Therefore a man shall forsake his father and his mother and cleave to his wife, and they shall become one flesh.
verses.2:25: And both of them were naked, the man and his wife, yet they felt no shame.
verses.3:1: Now the serpent was craftier than every beast of the field which the LORD God had made. And he said to the woman, "Has God indeed said, 'You shall not eat of any tree of the garden'?"
verses.3:2: And the woman said to the serpent, "Of the fruit of the trees of the garden we may eat;
verses.3:3: but of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God has said, 'You shall not eat of it, nor shall you touch it, lest you die.'"
verses.3:4: Then the serpent said to the woman, "You shall surely not die;
verses.3:5: for God knows that in the day you eat of it, your eyes shall be opened, and you shall be as God, knowing good and evil."
verses.3:6: And when the woman beheld that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was to be coveted to give wisdom, she took of its fruit and ate; and she gave also to her husband with her, and he ate.
verses.3:7: Then the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together and made for themselves girdles.
verses.3:8: And they heard the sound of the LORD God walking to and fro in the garden in the breeze of the day; and the man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God amidst the trees of the garden.
verses.3:9: Then the LORD God called to the man and said to him, "Where are you?"
verses.3:10: And he said, "I heard Your voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; therefore I hid myself."
verses.3:11: And He said, "Who declared to you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree from which I commanded you not to eat?"
verses.3:12: And the man said, "The woman whom You gave to be with me, she gave to me from the tree, and I ate."
verses.3:13: Then the LORD God said to the woman, "What is this that you have done?" And the woman said, "The serpent deceived me, and I ate."
verses.3:14: So the LORD God said to the serpent, "Because you have done this, cursed are you above all livestock and above every beast of the field; upon your belly you shall go, and dust you shall eat all the days of your life.
verses.3:15: And enmity I will set between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed: he shall strike your head, and you shall strike his heel."
verses.3:16: To the woman He said, "I will greatly multiply your sorrow and your conception; in pain you shall bear children; your desire shall be toward your husband, yet he shall rule over you."
verses.3:17: And to Adam He said, "Because you have heeded the voice of your wife, and have eaten from the tree concerning which I commanded you, saying, 'You shall not eat of it,' cursed is the ground on your account; in toil you shall eat of it all the days of your life.
verses.3:18: Thorns also and thistles it shall bring forth for you, and you shall eat the herb of the field.
verses.3:19: By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread, until you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken; for dust you are, and to dust you shall return."
verses.3:20: And the man called the name of his wife Eve, because she was the mother of all living.
verses.3:21: And the LORD God made for Adam and for his wife tunics of skin, and clothed them.
verses.3:22: Then the LORD God said, "Behold, the man has become as one of Us, knowing good and evil; and now, lest he stretch forth his hand and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever—"
verses.3:23: therefore the LORD God sent him forth from the garden of Eden to till the ground from which he had been taken.
verses.3:24: So He drove out the man; and He stationed at the east of the garden of Eden the cherubim, and the flaming blade of the revolving sword, to guard the way to the tree of life.
verses.4:1: Now Adam knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and bore Cain, and said, "I have acquired a man with the help of the LORD."
verses.4:2: And she bore again, his brother Abel. Now Abel became a shepherd of flocks, while Cain was a tiller of the ground.
verses.4:3: And it came to pass in the course of time that Cain brought an offering from the fruit of the ground to the LORD.
verses.4:4: And Abel also brought of the firstborn of his flock and of their fat. And the LORD showed regard for Abel and his offering,
verses.4:5: but for Cain and his offering He showed no regard. And Cain was exceedingly angry, and his countenance fell.
verses.4:6: Then the LORD said to Cain, "Why are you angered, and why has your countenance fallen?
verses.4:7: If you do well, shall you not be accepted? Yet if you do not do well, sin crouches at the door; its desire is toward you, but you must rule over it."
verses.4:8: And Cain spoke to Abel his brother; and it came to pass, while they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother and slew him.
verses.4:9: Then the LORD said to Cain, "Where is your brother Abel?" And he replied, "I do not know. Am I the keeper of my brother?"
verses.4:10: And He said, "What have you done? The voice of your brother's blood cries out to Me from the ground.
verses.4:11: Now therefore you are cursed from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive the blood of your brother from your hand.
verses.4:12: When you till the ground, it shall no longer yield its strength to you; a fugitive and a wanderer you shall be upon the earth."
verses.4:13: And Cain said to the LORD, "My punishment is too great to bear.
verses.4:14: Behold, You have driven me out this day from the face of the ground, and from Your presence I shall be hidden; I shall be a fugitive and a wanderer upon the earth, and whoever finds me will slay me."
verses.4:15: And the LORD said to him, "Therefore, whoever slays Cain, vengeance shall be exacted on him sevenfold." And the LORD appointed a mark for Cain, lest anyone who found him should strike him down.
verses.4:16: So Cain departed from the presence of the LORD and dwelt in the land of Nod, to the east of Eden.
verses.4:17: And Cain knew his wife, and she conceived and bore Enoch. And he built a city, and he called the name of the city after the name of his son, Enoch.
verses.4:18: To Enoch was born Irad; and Irad fathered Mehujael, and Mehujael fathered Methushael, and Methushael fathered Lamech.
verses.4:19: And Lamech took for himself two wives: the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the second was Zillah.
verses.4:20: And Adah bore Jabal; he was the father of those who dwell in tents and keep livestock.
verses.4:21: His brother's name was Jubal; he was the father of all who play the lyre and pipe.
verses.4:22: Zillah also bore Tubal-Cain, the forger of every instrument of bronze and iron; and the sister of Tubal-Cain was Naamah.
verses.4:23: Then Lamech said to his wives, "Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; wives of Lamech, give ear to my speech! For I have slain a man for wounding me, and a young man for bruising me.
verses.4:24: If Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold."
verses.4:25: And Adam knew his wife again, and she bore a son and called his name Seth, "For God has appointed for me another seed in place of Abel, because Cain slew him."
verses.4:26: And to Seth also a son was born, and he called his name Enosh. At that time men began to call upon the name of the LORD.
verses.5:1: This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God He made him.
verses.5:2: Male and female He created them, and He blessed them and called their name Man in the day they were created.
verses.5:3: And Adam lived one hundred and thirty years, and fathered a son in his own likeness, after his image, and called his name Seth.
verses.5:4: And the days of Adam after he fathered Seth were eight hundred years; and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.5:5: So all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years; and he died.
verses.5:6: And Seth lived one hundred and five years, and fathered Enosh.
verses.5:7: And Seth lived after he fathered Enosh eight hundred and seven years, and fathered sons and daughters.
verses.5:8: So all the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years; and he died.
verses.5:9: And Enosh lived ninety years, and fathered Kenan.
verses.5:10: And Enosh lived after he fathered Kenan eight hundred and fifteen years, and fathered sons and daughters.
verses.5:11: So all the days of Enosh were nine hundred and five years; and he died.
verses.5:12: And Kenan lived seventy years, and fathered Mahalalel.
verses.5:13: And Kenan lived after he fathered Mahalalel eight hundred and forty years, and fathered sons and daughters.
verses.5:14: So all the days of Kenan were nine hundred and ten years; and he died.
verses.5:15: And Mahalalel lived sixty-five years, and fathered Jared.
verses.5:16: And Mahalalel lived after he fathered Jared eight hundred and thirty years, and fathered sons and daughters.
verses.5:17: So all the days of Mahalalel were eight hundred and ninety-five years; and he died.
verses.5:18: And Jared lived one hundred and sixty-two years, and fathered Enoch.
verses.5:19: And Jared lived after he fathered Enoch eight hundred years, and fathered sons and daughters.
verses.5:20: So all the days of Jared were nine hundred and sixty-two years; and he died.
verses.5:21: And Enoch lived sixty-five years, and fathered Methuselah.
verses.5:22: And Enoch walked with God after he fathered Methuselah three hundred years, and fathered sons and daughters.
verses.5:23: So all the days of Enoch were three hundred and sixty-five years.
verses.5:24: And Enoch walked with God, and he was no more, for God took him.
verses.5:25: And Methuselah lived one hundred and eighty-seven years, and fathered Lamech.
verses.5:26: And Methuselah lived after he fathered Lamech seven hundred and eighty-two years, and fathered sons and daughters.
verses.5:27: So all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred and sixty-nine years; and he died.
verses.5:28: And Lamech lived one hundred and eighty-two years, and fathered a son.
verses.5:29: And he called his name Noah, saying, "This one shall comfort us from our labor and the painful toil of our hands, arising from the ground that the LORD has cursed."
verses.5:30: And Lamech lived after he fathered Noah five hundred and ninety-five years, and fathered sons and daughters.
verses.5:31: So all the days of Lamech were seven hundred and seventy-seven years; and he died.
verses.5:32: And Noah was five hundred years old, and Noah fathered Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
verses.6:1: And it came to pass, when mankind began to multiply upon the face of the ground, and daughters were born to them,
verses.6:2: that the sons of God beheld the daughters of men, that they were fair; and they took for themselves wives from among all whom they chose.
verses.6:3: And the LORD said, "My Spirit shall not abide in man forever, since he indeed is flesh; and his days shall be one hundred and twenty years."
verses.6:4: The Nephilim were upon the earth in those days, and also afterward, when the sons of God went in to the daughters of men and they bore offspring to them; those were the mighty men from of old, the men of renown.
verses.6:5: And the LORD saw that the wickedness of man was multiplied upon the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil all the day long.
verses.6:6: And the LORD regretted that He had made man upon the earth, and He was pained in His heart.
verses.6:7: And the LORD said, "I will blot out man whom I have created from off the face of the ground—from man to beast, to creeping thing, and to the birds of the heavens—for I regret that I have made them."
verses.6:8: Yet Noah found favor in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.6:9: These are the generations of Noah: Noah was a righteous man, blameless among his generations; with God Noah walked.
verses.6:10: And Noah fathered three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
verses.6:11: Now the earth became corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.
verses.6:12: And God saw the earth, and behold, it was corrupted; for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth.
verses.6:13: And God said to Noah, "The end of all flesh has come before Me, for the earth is filled with violence because of them; and behold, I am about to destroy them together with the earth.
verses.6:14: Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood; you shall make compartments in the ark, and you shall coat it within and without with pitch.
verses.6:15: And this is the manner in which you shall make it: three hundred cubits shall be the length of the ark, fifty cubits its breadth, and thirty cubits its height.
verses.6:16: You shall make a window for the ark, and finish it to a cubit from above; and the doorway of the ark you shall set in its side. With lower, second, and third stories you shall make it.
verses.6:17: And as for Me, behold, I am bringing the flood of waters upon the earth to destroy all flesh in which is the breath of life from under the heavens; all that is upon the earth shall expire.
verses.6:18: Yet I will establish My covenant with you; and you shall enter the ark—you, your sons, your wife, and the wives of your sons with you.
verses.6:19: And of every living thing of all flesh, two of every kind you shall bring into the ark, to preserve them alive with you; male and female they shall be.
verses.6:20: Of the birds according to their kind, of the cattle according to their kind, and of every creeping thing of the ground according to its kind, two of every kind shall come to you to be preserved alive.
verses.6:21: And as for you, take for yourself of all food that is eaten, and gather it to yourself; and it shall be for food to you and to them."
verses.6:22: So Noah did; according to everything that God commanded him, thus he did.
verses.7:1: And the LORD said to Noah, "Enter the ark, you and all your household, for you I have seen to be righteous before Me in this generation.
verses.7:2: Of every clean beast you shall take for yourself seven each, a male and his mate; and of the beasts that are not clean, two, a male and his mate;
verses.7:3: also of the birds of the heavens, seven each, male and female, to preserve offspring alive upon the face of all the earth.
verses.7:4: For after seven days more, I will send rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights, and I will blot out every living thing that I have made from the face of the ground."
verses.7:5: So Noah did according to everything that the LORD commanded him.
verses.7:6: Now Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters came upon the earth.
verses.7:7: And Noah went into the ark, together with his sons, his wife, and the wives of his sons, because of the waters of the flood.
verses.7:8: Of the clean beasts, and of the beasts that are not clean, and of the birds, and of everything that creeps upon the ground,
verses.7:9: two by two they came to Noah into the ark, male and female, just as God had commanded Noah.
verses.7:10: And it came to pass at the end of the seven days that the waters of the flood came upon the earth.
verses.7:11: In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that day all the fountains of the great deep burst open, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.
verses.7:12: And the rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.
verses.7:13: On that very day Noah entered the ark, together with Shem, Ham, and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and the wife of Noah and the three wives of his sons with them—
verses.7:14: they, and every wild beast according to its kind, and all the livestock according to their kind, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth according to its kind, and every bird according to its kind, every bird of every wing.
verses.7:15: And they came to Noah into the ark, two by two of all flesh in which was the breath of life.
verses.7:16: And those that came in entered, male and female of all flesh, just as God had commanded him; and the LORD shut him in.
verses.7:17: And the flood was forty days upon the earth; and the waters multiplied and bore up the ark, so that it rose above the earth.
verses.7:18: And the waters prevailed and multiplied exceedingly upon the earth, and the ark floated upon the face of the waters.
verses.7:19: And the waters prevailed most exceedingly upon the earth, and all the high mountains beneath all the heavens were covered.
verses.7:20: Fifteen cubits higher the waters prevailed, so that the mountains were covered.
verses.7:21: And all flesh that moved upon the earth perished—birds, livestock, wild beasts, and every swarming thing that swarms upon the earth, and all mankind.
verses.7:22: Every creature that had the breath of the spirit of life in its nostrils, of all that were on the dry land, died.
verses.7:23: And He blotted out every living thing that was upon the face of the ground—from man to beast, to creeping thing, and to the birds of the heavens—and they were blotted out from the earth; and only Noah remained, and those who were with him in the ark.
verses.7:24: And the waters prevailed upon the earth for one hundred and fifty days.
verses.8:1: Then God remembered Noah, and every wild beast and all the livestock that were with him in the ark; and God caused a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided.
verses.8:2: And the fountains of the deep and the floodgates of the heavens were stopped up, and the rain from the heavens was held back.
verses.8:3: And the waters receded steadily from off the earth; and at the end of one hundred and fifty days the waters had diminished.
verses.8:4: And the ark came to rest in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat.
verses.8:5: And the waters continued to diminish until the tenth month; in the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the summits of the mountains became visible.
verses.8:6: And it came to pass, at the close of forty days, that Noah opened the window of the ark that he had made.
verses.8:7: And he sent forth a raven, and it went out, going to and fro until the waters had dried up from off the earth.
verses.8:8: Then he sent forth a dove from himself to see whether the waters had abated from the face of the ground.
verses.8:9: But the dove found no resting place for the sole of her foot, so she returned to him into the ark, for waters were upon the face of the whole earth. Then he reached out his hand, took her, and brought her to himself into the ark.
verses.8:10: Then he waited still another seven days, and once more he sent forth the dove out of the ark.
verses.8:11: And the dove came to him toward evening, and behold, a freshly plucked olive leaf was in her beak; thus Noah knew that the waters had abated from the earth.
verses.8:12: And he waited still another seven days and sent forth the dove, and she did not return to him anymore.
verses.8:13: Now it came to pass in the six hundred and first year, in the first month, on the first day of the month, that the waters had dried up from off the earth. Then Noah removed the covering of the ark and looked, and behold, the face of the ground was dry.
verses.8:14: And in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth had become dry.
verses.8:15: And God spoke to Noah, saying,
verses.8:16: "Come forth from the ark, you and your wife, and your sons and the wives of your sons with you.
verses.8:17: Bring forth with you every living creature of all flesh that is with you—birds, livestock, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth—that they may teem in the earth, and be fruitful and multiply upon the earth."
verses.8:18: So Noah came forth, and his sons, his wife, and the wives of his sons with him.
verses.8:19: Every wild beast, every creeping thing, and every bird—everything that moves upon the earth—according to their families, came forth from the ark.
verses.8:20: And Noah built an altar to the LORD, and he took from every clean beast and from every clean bird, and offered up burnt offerings upon the altar.
verses.8:21: And the LORD smelled the soothing aroma, and the LORD said in His heart, "I will never again curse the ground on account of man, for the inclination of the heart of man is evil from his youth; nor will I again strike down every living thing as I have done.
verses.8:22: For all the remaining days of the earth, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease."
verses.9:1: And God blessed Noah and his sons, and He said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth.
verses.9:2: And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth and upon every bird of the heavens; with all that creeps upon the ground and with all the fish of the sea, into your hand they are delivered.
verses.9:3: Every moving creature that is alive shall be food for you; even as the green plants, I have given all things to you.
verses.9:4: Yet flesh with its life—its blood—you shall not eat.
verses.9:5: And surely for your lifeblood I will demand a reckoning; from the hand of every beast I will require it, and from the hand of man—from the hand of each man for his brother—I will require the life of man.
verses.9:6: He who sheds the blood of man, by man his blood shall be shed; for in the image of God He made man.
verses.9:7: And as for you, be fruitful and multiply; teem upon the earth and multiply in it."
verses.9:8: Then God spoke to Noah and to his sons with him, saying,
verses.9:9: "And as for Me, behold, I establish My covenant with you and with your seed after you,
verses.9:10: and with every living creature that is with you—the birds, the livestock, and every beast of the earth with you—from all that came out of the ark to every beast of the earth.
verses.9:11: I establish My covenant with you, that never again shall all flesh be cut off by the waters of the flood, and never again shall there be a flood to destroy the earth."
verses.9:12: And God said, "This is the sign of the covenant that I give between Me and you, and between every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations:
verses.9:13: My bow I have placed in the cloud, and it shall be for a sign of the covenant between Me and the earth.
verses.9:14: And it shall come to pass, when I bring a cloud over the earth, that the bow shall be seen in the cloud,
verses.9:15: and I will remember My covenant that is between Me and you and every living creature of all flesh; and the waters shall never again become a flood to destroy all flesh.
verses.9:16: When the bow is in the cloud, I will look upon it to remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is upon the earth."
verses.9:17: And God said to Noah, "This is the sign of the covenant that I have established between Me and all flesh that is upon the earth."
verses.9:18: Now the sons of Noah who went forth from the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth; and Ham was the father of Canaan.
verses.9:19: These three were the sons of Noah, and from these the whole earth was dispersed.
verses.9:20: And Noah began to be a man of the soil, and he planted a vineyard.
verses.9:21: And he drank of the wine and became drunk, and he uncovered himself within his tent.
verses.9:22: And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and he told his two brothers outside.
verses.9:23: Then Shem and Japheth took the garment, laid it upon the shoulders of both of them, and walked backward and covered the nakedness of their father; and their faces were turned backward, so they did not see their father's nakedness.
verses.9:24: Then Noah awoke from his wine, and he knew what his youngest son had done to him.
verses.9:25: And he said, "Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants he shall be to his brethren."
verses.9:26: He also said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem, and let Canaan be a servant to him.
verses.9:27: May God enlarge Japheth, and may he dwell in the tents of Shem; and let Canaan be a servant to him."
verses.9:28: And Noah lived after the flood three hundred and fifty years.
verses.9:29: So all the days of Noah were nine hundred and fifty years, and he died.
verses.10:1: Now these are the generations of the sons of Noah: Shem, Ham, and Japheth; and sons were born to them after the flood.
verses.10:2: The sons of Japheth were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
verses.10:3: And the sons of Gomer were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
verses.10:4: And the sons of Javan were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
verses.10:5: From these the coastlands of the nations were separated into their lands, each according to his tongue, according to their families, in their nations.
verses.10:6: And the sons of Ham were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
verses.10:7: And the sons of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca; and the sons of Raamah were Sheba and Dedan.
verses.10:8: And Cush fathered Nimrod; he began to be a mighty one upon the earth.
verses.10:9: He was a mighty hunter before the LORD; therefore it is said, "Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD."
verses.10:10: And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
verses.10:11: From that land he went forth into Assyria and built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, Calah,
verses.10:12: and Resen, between Nineveh and Calah; that is the great city.
verses.10:13: And Mizraim fathered Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
verses.10:14: Pathrusim, Casluhim—from whom the Philistines came forth—and Caphtorim.
verses.10:15: And Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn, and Heth,
verses.10:16: the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,
verses.10:17: the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,
verses.10:18: the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites; and afterward the families of the Canaanites were dispersed.
verses.10:19: And the border of the Canaanites extended from Sidon, as you go toward Gerar, as far as Gaza; and as you go toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.
verses.10:20: These were the sons of Ham, according to their families, according to their tongues, in their lands and in their nations.
verses.10:21: And to Shem also children were born, the father of all the children of Eber, the brother of Japheth the elder.
verses.10:22: The sons of Shem were Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.
verses.10:23: And the sons of Aram were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
verses.10:24: And Arpachshad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.
verses.10:25: And to Eber were born two sons: the name of the one was Peleg, for in his days the earth was divided, and his brother's name was Joktan.
verses.10:26: And Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
verses.10:29: Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab; all these were the sons of Joktan.
verses.10:30: And their dwelling place extended from Mesha, as you go toward Sephar, the mountain of the east.
verses.10:31: These were the sons of Shem, according to their families, according to their tongues, in their lands, according to their nations.
verses.10:32: These were the families of the sons of Noah, according to their generations, in their nations; and from these the nations were separated upon the earth after the flood.
verses.11:1: Now all the earth had one language and common words.
verses.11:2: And it happened, as they journeyed from the east, that they found a broad plain in the land of Shinar, and they settled there.
verses.11:3: Then they said one to another, "Come, let us mold bricks and burn them thoroughly." So brick served them for stone, and bitumen served them for mortar.
verses.11:4: And they said, "Come, let us build for ourselves a city and a tower with its summit in the heavens, and let us make a name for ourselves, lest we be dispersed over the face of all the earth."
verses.11:5: Then the LORD descended to see the city and the tower that the sons of men had built.
verses.11:6: And the LORD said, "Behold, they are one people and all of them have one language, and this is what they have begun to do; and now nothing that they purpose to do will be withheld from them.
verses.11:7: Come, let Us go down and confound their language there, so that one may not understand the speech of another."
verses.11:8: So the LORD dispersed them from there over the face of all the earth, and they ceased building the city.
verses.11:9: Therefore its name was called Babel, because there the LORD confounded the language of all the earth; and from there the LORD dispersed them over the face of all the earth.
verses.11:10: These are the generations of Shem: Shem was one hundred years old, and he fathered Arpachshad two years after the flood.
verses.11:11: And Shem lived five hundred years after he fathered Arpachshad, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.11:12: Now Arpachshad lived thirty-five years, and he fathered Shelah.
verses.11:13: And Arpachshad lived four hundred and three years after he fathered Shelah, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.11:14: Now Shelah lived thirty years, and he fathered Eber.
verses.11:15: And Shelah lived four hundred and three years after he fathered Eber, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.11:16: And Eber lived thirty-four years, and he fathered Peleg.
verses.11:17: And Eber lived four hundred and thirty years after he fathered Peleg, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.11:18: And Peleg lived thirty years, and he fathered Reu.
verses.11:19: And Peleg lived two hundred and nine years after he fathered Reu, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.11:20: And Reu lived thirty-two years, and he fathered Serug.
verses.11:21: And Reu lived two hundred and seven years after he fathered Serug, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.11:22: And Serug lived thirty years, and he fathered Nahor.
verses.11:23: And Serug lived two hundred years after he fathered Nahor, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.11:24: And Nahor lived twenty-nine years, and he fathered Terah.
verses.11:25: And Nahor lived one hundred and nineteen years after he fathered Terah, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.11:26: And Terah lived seventy years, and he fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
verses.11:27: Now these are the generations of Terah: Terah fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran; and Haran fathered Lot.
verses.11:28: And Haran died in the presence of his father Terah in the land of his nativity, in Ur of the Chaldeans.
verses.11:29: Then Abram and Nahor took wives for themselves: the name of Abram's wife was Sarai, and the name of Nahor's wife was Milcah, the daughter of Haran, the father of Milcah and the father of Iscah.
verses.11:30: Now Sarai was barren; she had no child.
verses.11:31: And Terah took his son Abram, and Lot the son of Haran, his son's son, and his daughter-in-law Sarai, the wife of his son Abram; and they set out with them from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan, and they came to Haran and settled there.
verses.11:32: And the days of Terah were two hundred and five years; and Terah died in Haran.
verses.12:1: Now the LORD said to Abram, "Depart from your land, and from your kindred, and from your father's house, to the land that I will show you.
verses.12:2: And I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you and magnify your name, and you shall be a blessing.
verses.12:3: I will bless those who bless you, and the one who curses you I will curse; and in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed."
verses.12:4: So Abram departed as the LORD had spoken to him, and Lot went with him. Now Abram was seventy-five years old when he went out from Haran.
verses.12:5: And Abram took his wife Sarai, and Lot his brother's son, and all their possessions that they had gathered, and the people whom they had acquired in Haran; and they set out to go to the land of Canaan, and they came into the land of Canaan.
verses.12:6: Then Abram passed through the land as far as the place of Shechem, to the terebinth of Moreh. At that time the Canaanites were in the land.
verses.12:7: And the LORD appeared to Abram and said, "To your seed I will give this land." So he built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him.
verses.12:8: And he moved on from there to the hill country east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east; and there he built an altar to the LORD and called upon the name of the LORD.
verses.12:9: Then Abram journeyed on, continuing by stages toward the Negev.
verses.12:10: Now there was a famine in the land, and Abram went down to Egypt to sojourn there, for the famine was severe in the land.
verses.12:11: And it came to pass, as he drew near to enter Egypt, that he said to his wife Sarai, "Behold now, I know that you are a woman beautiful in appearance.
verses.12:12: Therefore it shall come to pass, when the Egyptians see you, that they will say, 'This is his wife,' and they will slay me, but they will keep you alive.
verses.12:13: Please say that you are my sister, so that it may go well with me for your sake, and my soul may live on your account."
verses.12:14: And so it was, when Abram entered Egypt, that the Egyptians saw the woman, that she was exceedingly beautiful.
verses.12:15: The princes of Pharaoh also saw her and praised her to Pharaoh, and the woman was taken into Pharaoh's house.
verses.12:16: And he dealt well with Abram for her sake; and he had flocks and herds, male donkeys, male and female servants, female donkeys, and camels.
verses.12:17: But the LORD struck Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram's wife.
verses.12:18: Then Pharaoh summoned Abram and said, "What is this that you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she was your wife?
verses.12:19: Why did you say, 'She is my sister,' so that I took her to be my wife? Now therefore, behold, here is your wife; take her and go!"
verses.12:20: So Pharaoh gave men orders concerning him, and they sent him away, along with his wife and all that he possessed.
verses.13:1: Then Abram went up out of Egypt, he and his wife and all that belonged to him, and Lot with him, into the Negev.
verses.13:2: Now Abram was exceedingly wealthy in livestock, in silver, and in gold.
verses.13:3: And he went on his journeys from the Negev as far as Bethel, to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai,
verses.13:4: to the place of the altar that he had made there at the first; and there Abram called upon the name of the LORD.
verses.13:5: Lot also, who went with Abram, had flocks and herds and tents.
verses.13:6: And the land could not support them to dwell together, for their possessions were so great that they were not able to dwell together.
verses.13:7: And there arose strife between the herdsmen of Abram's livestock and the herdsmen of Lot's livestock. At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were dwelling in the land.
verses.13:8: So Abram said to Lot, "Please let there be no strife between me and you, and between my herdsmen and your herdsmen, for we are brethren.
verses.13:9: Is not the whole land before you? Please separate yourself from me: if you go to the left, then I will go to the right; and if you go to the right, then I will go to the left."
verses.13:10: Then Lot lifted up his eyes and beheld all the plain of the Jordan, that it was everywhere well watered—before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah—like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt, as you go toward Zoar.
verses.13:11: So Lot chose for himself all the plain of the Jordan, and Lot journeyed eastward. Thus they separated one from the other.
verses.13:12: Abram dwelt in the land of Canaan, while Lot dwelt among the cities of the plain and moved his tents as far as Sodom.
verses.13:13: Now the men of Sodom were exceedingly wicked and sinful against the LORD.
verses.13:14: And the LORD said to Abram, after Lot had separated from him, "Lift up your eyes now and look from the place where you are—northward, and southward, and eastward, and westward;
verses.13:15: for all the land that you see I will give to you and to your seed forever.
verses.13:16: And I will make your seed like the dust of the earth, so that if a man can number the dust of the earth, then your seed also shall be numbered.
verses.13:17: Arise, walk through the land in its length and in its breadth, for to you I will give it."
verses.13:18: Then Abram moved his tents, and came and dwelt by the terebinths of Mamre, which are in Hebron, and there he built an altar to the LORD.
verses.14:1: Now it came to pass in the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim,
verses.14:2: that they waged war against Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela—that is, Zoar.
verses.14:3: All these joined forces at the Valley of Siddim—that is, the Salt Sea.
verses.14:4: For twelve years they served Chedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
verses.14:5: And in the fourteenth year Chedorlaomer came, along with the kings who were with him, and they struck down the Rephaim in Ashteroth Karnaim, the Zuzim in Ham, the Emim in Shaveh Kiriathaim,
verses.14:6: and the Horites in their hill country of Seir, as far as El Paran, which is beside the wilderness.
verses.14:7: Then they turned back and came to En Mishpat—that is, Kadesh—and struck all the territory of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites who dwelt in Hazazon Tamar.
verses.14:8: Then the king of Sodom marched out, with the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela—that is, Zoar—and they arrayed themselves for battle against them in the Valley of Siddim:
verses.14:9: against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goiim, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar—four kings against the five.
verses.14:10: Now the Valley of Siddim was filled with bitumen pits; and the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled and fell into them, while those who remained fled to the mountains.
verses.14:11: So they seized all the possessions of Sodom and Gomorrah, and all their provisions, and departed.
verses.14:12: They also took Lot, the son of Abram's brother, along with his possessions, and departed, for he was dwelling in Sodom.
verses.14:13: Then one who had escaped came and reported it to Abram the Hebrew, for he was dwelling by the terebinths of Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshcol and brother of Aner; and they were allies of Abram by covenant.
verses.14:14: When Abram heard that his kinsman had been taken captive, he mustered his trained men, born in his own house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued as far as Dan.
verses.14:15: He divided his men against them by night, he and his servants, and struck them down, and pursued them as far as Hobah, which lies north of Damascus.
verses.14:16: So he brought back all the possessions, and also brought back his kinsman Lot and his possessions, as well as the women and the people.
verses.14:17: And after his return from striking down Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him, the king of Sodom went out to meet him at the Valley of Shaveh—that is, the King's Valley.
verses.14:18: And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine; now he was priest of God Most High.
verses.14:19: And he blessed him and said, "Blessed be Abram by God Most High, Possessor of heaven and earth;
verses.14:20: and blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your adversaries into your hand." And he gave him a tenth of everything.
verses.14:21: Now the king of Sodom said to Abram, "Give me the people, and take the possessions for yourself."
verses.14:22: But Abram replied to the king of Sodom, "I have lifted up my hand to the LORD, God Most High, Possessor of heaven and earth,
verses.14:23: that I will not take even a thread or a sandal strap, nor anything that belongs to you, lest you say, 'I have made Abram rich'—
verses.14:24: nothing for myself, except only what the young men have eaten, and the share of the men who went with me—Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre; let them take their share."
verses.15:1: After these things the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision, saying, "Do not be afraid, Abram; I am a shield to you, and your reward shall be exceedingly great."
verses.15:2: But Abram said, "Lord GOD, what will You give me, since I go on childless, and the heir of my household is Eliezer of Damascus?"
verses.15:3: And Abram said, "Behold, You have given me no offspring, and indeed one born in my household is my heir."
verses.15:4: And behold, the word of the LORD came to him, saying, "This one shall not be your heir; rather, one who comes forth from your own body shall be your heir."
verses.15:5: Then He brought him outside and said, "Look now toward the heavens, and count the stars, if you are able to number them." And He said to him, "So shall your offspring be."
verses.15:6: And he believed in the LORD, and He reckoned it to him for righteousness.
verses.15:7: Then He said to him, "I am the LORD, who brought you out from Ur of the Chaldeans, to give you this land to possess it."
verses.15:8: And he said, "Lord GOD, by what shall I know that I shall possess it?"
verses.15:9: And He said to him, "Take for Me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old she-goat, a three-year-old ram, a turtledove, and a young pigeon."
verses.15:10: So he brought all these to Him and cut them in two down the middle, and placed each piece opposite its counterpart; but he did not cut the birds in two.
verses.15:11: And birds of prey swooped down upon the carcasses, but Abram drove them away.
verses.15:12: Now as the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and behold, a dreadful, great darkness fell upon him.
verses.15:13: Then He said to Abram, "Know for certain that your offspring will be sojourners in a land that is not theirs, and will be in servitude to them, and they will afflict them four hundred years.
verses.15:14: Yet I will also judge the nation whom they serve, and afterward they shall come out with great possessions.
verses.15:15: As for you, you shall go to your fathers in peace; you shall be buried at a good old age.
verses.15:16: And in the fourth generation they shall return here, for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete."
verses.15:17: And it came to pass, when the sun had gone down and thick darkness had fallen, that behold, a smoking oven and a blazing torch passed between those pieces.
verses.15:18: On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, "To your offspring I have given this land, from the river of Egypt as far as the great river, the river Euphrates—
verses.15:19: the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites,
verses.15:20: the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaim,
verses.15:21: the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites."
verses.16:1: Now Sarai, Abram's wife, had borne him no children. And she had an Egyptian maidservant whose name was Hagar.
verses.16:2: So Sarai said to Abram, "Behold now, the LORD has restrained me from bearing children. Please go in to my maidservant; perhaps I shall be built up through her." And Abram heeded the voice of Sarai.
verses.16:3: Then Sarai, Abram's wife, took Hagar the Egyptian, her maidservant, after Abram had dwelt ten years in the land of Canaan, and gave her to her husband Abram to be his wife.
verses.16:4: So he went in to Hagar, and she conceived. And when she saw that she had conceived, her mistress became lightly esteemed in her eyes.
verses.16:5: Then Sarai said to Abram, "May the wrong done to me be upon you! I gave my maidservant into your embrace; and when she saw that she had conceived, I became lightly esteemed in her eyes. May the LORD judge between me and you!"
verses.16:6: So Abram said to Sarai, "Behold, your maidservant is in your hand; do to her what is good in your eyes." And Sarai afflicted her, and she fled from her presence.
verses.16:7: Now the Angel of the LORD found her by a spring of water in the wilderness, by the spring on the way to Shur.
verses.16:8: And He said, "Hagar, Sarai's maidservant, where have you come from, and where are you going?" And she said, "I am fleeing from the presence of my mistress Sarai."
verses.16:9: Then the Angel of the LORD said to her, "Return to your mistress, and submit yourself under her hand."
verses.16:10: And the Angel of the LORD said to her, "I will greatly multiply your offspring, so that they cannot be numbered for multitude."
verses.16:11: And the Angel of the LORD said to her, "Behold, you are with child and shall bear a son; you shall name him Ishmael, for the LORD has heard your affliction.
verses.16:12: He shall be a wild donkey of a man; his hand shall be against every man, and every man's hand against him, and he shall dwell over against all his brethren."
verses.16:13: Then she called the name of the LORD who spoke to her, "You are the God who sees," for she said, "Have I indeed here looked after Him who sees me?"
verses.16:14: Therefore the well was called Beer Lahai Roi; behold, it lies between Kadesh and Bered.
verses.16:15: So Hagar bore Abram a son; and Abram called the name of his son, whom Hagar bore, Ishmael.
verses.16:16: Now Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.
verses.17:1: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to Abram and said to him, "I am God Almighty; walk before Me and be blameless.
verses.17:2: And I will set My covenant between Me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly."
verses.17:3: Then Abram fell upon his face, and God spoke with him, saying,
verses.17:4: "As for Me, behold, My covenant is with you, and you shall become the father of a multitude of nations.
verses.17:5: No longer shall your name be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham; for I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.
verses.17:6: And I will make you exceedingly fruitful, and I will make nations of you, and kings shall come forth from you.
verses.17:7: And I will establish My covenant between Me and you and your seed after you throughout their generations, for an everlasting covenant, to be God to you and to your seed after you.
verses.17:8: Also I will give to you and to your seed after you the land of your sojournings, all the land of Canaan, as an everlasting possession; and I will be their God."
verses.17:9: And God said to Abraham, "As for you, you shall keep My covenant, you and your seed after you throughout their generations.
verses.17:10: This is My covenant which you shall keep, between Me and you and your seed after you: every male among you shall be circumcised.
verses.17:11: And you shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between Me and you.
verses.17:12: He who is eight days old among you shall be circumcised, every male throughout your generations, both he who is born in the house and he who is bought with silver from any foreigner who is not of your seed.
verses.17:13: He who is born in your house and he who is bought with your silver shall surely be circumcised; and My covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.
verses.17:14: And the uncircumcised male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin, that soul shall be cut off from his people; he has broken My covenant."
verses.17:15: Then God said to Abraham, "As for Sarai your wife, you shall not call her name Sarai, for Sarah shall be her name.
verses.17:16: And I will bless her, and moreover I will give you a son by her; yes, I will bless her, and she shall become nations; kings of peoples shall come from her."
verses.17:17: Then Abraham fell upon his face and laughed, and said in his heart, "Shall a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? And shall Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear a child?"
verses.17:18: And Abraham said to God, "Oh, that Ishmael might live before You!"
verses.17:19: Then God said, "No, indeed, Sarah your wife shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac; and I will establish My covenant with him for an everlasting covenant, and for his seed after him.
verses.17:20: And as for Ishmael, I have heard you. Behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him exceedingly. He shall father twelve princes, and I will make him a great nation.
verses.17:21: But My covenant I will establish with Isaac, whom Sarah shall bear to you at this appointed time next year."
verses.17:22: When He finished speaking with him, God ascended from Abraham.
verses.17:23: So Abraham took Ishmael his son, and all who were born in his house, and all who were bought with his silver, every male among the men of Abraham's house, and circumcised the flesh of their foreskins on that very same day, just as God had spoken with him.
verses.17:24: Now Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
verses.17:25: And Ishmael his son was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
verses.17:26: On that very same day Abraham was circumcised, and Ishmael his son.
verses.17:27: And all the men of his house, whether born in the house or bought with silver from a foreigner, were circumcised with him.
verses.18:1: Then the LORD appeared to him by the terebinths of Mamre, as he was sitting at the entrance of the tent in the heat of the day.
verses.18:2: And he lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, three men were standing near him; and when he saw them, he ran from the entrance of the tent to meet them, and bowed himself to the ground,
verses.18:3: and said, "My Lord, if now I have found favor in Your sight, please do not pass by Your servant.
verses.18:4: Please let a little water be brought, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree.
verses.18:5: And I will bring a morsel of bread, and sustain your hearts; after that you may pass on, since for this reason you have come by your servant." And they said, "Do just as you have spoken."
verses.18:6: So Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah and said, "Hurry! Take three measures of fine flour, knead it, and make cakes."
verses.18:7: And Abraham ran to the herd, took a calf, tender and good, and gave it to a young man, who hurried to prepare it.
verses.18:8: Then he took curds and milk and the calf which he had prepared, and set them before them; and he stood beside them under the tree while they ate.
verses.18:9: Then they said to him, "Where is Sarah your wife?" And he said, "Behold, in the tent."
verses.18:10: And He said, "I will surely return to you according to the time of life, and behold, Sarah your wife shall have a son." Now Sarah was listening at the entrance of the tent, which was behind Him.
verses.18:11: Now Abraham and Sarah were old, advanced in days; it had ceased to be with Sarah after the manner of women.
verses.18:12: Therefore Sarah laughed within herself, saying, "After I have grown old, shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also?"
verses.18:13: And the LORD said to Abraham, "Why did Sarah laugh, saying, 'Shall I indeed bear a child, now that I am old?'
verses.18:14: Is anything too wondrous for the LORD? At the appointed time I will return to you, according to the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son."
verses.18:15: But Sarah denied it, saying, "I did not laugh," for she was afraid. And He said, "No, but you did laugh."
verses.18:16: Then the men rose up from there and looked down toward Sodom, and Abraham walked with them to send them on their way.
verses.18:17: And the LORD said, "Shall I conceal from Abraham what I am doing,
verses.18:18: since Abraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him?
verses.18:19: For I have known him, in order that he may command his sons and his household after him, that they keep the way of the LORD, to do righteousness and justice, so that the LORD may bring to Abraham what He has spoken concerning him."
verses.18:20: And the LORD said, "Because the outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and because their sin is very grievous,
verses.18:21: I will go down now and see whether they have done altogether according to the outcry against it that has come to Me; and if not, I will know."
verses.18:22: Then the men turned away from there and went toward Sodom, while Abraham still stood before the LORD.
verses.18:23: And Abraham drew near and said, "Will You indeed sweep away the righteous with the wicked?
verses.18:24: Suppose there are fifty righteous within the city; will You indeed sweep it away and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous who are in its midst?
verses.18:25: Far be it from You to do such a thing as this, to put the righteous to death with the wicked, so that the righteous should be as the wicked; far be it from You! Shall the Judge of all the earth not do justice?"
verses.18:26: So the LORD said, "If I find in Sodom fifty righteous within the city, then I will spare the whole place for their sake."
verses.18:27: Then Abraham answered and said, "Behold now, I have undertaken to speak to the Lord, though I am but dust and ashes:
verses.18:28: suppose the fifty righteous lack five; will You destroy the whole city for the lack of five?" And He said, "I will not destroy it if I find forty-five there."
verses.18:29: And he spoke to Him yet again and said, "Suppose forty are found there." And He said, "I will not do it for the sake of the forty."
verses.18:30: Then he said, "Oh, do not let the Lord be angry, and I will speak: suppose thirty are found there." And He said, "I will not do it if I find thirty there."
verses.18:31: And he said, "Behold now, I have undertaken to speak to the Lord: suppose twenty are found there." And He said, "I will not destroy it for the sake of the twenty."
verses.18:32: Then he said, "Oh, do not let the Lord be angry, and I will speak yet this once: suppose ten are found there." And He said, "I will not destroy it for the sake of the ten."
verses.18:33: So the LORD departed as soon as He had finished speaking to Abraham, and Abraham returned to his place.
verses.19:1: And the two angels came to Sodom at evening, while Lot was sitting at the gate of Sodom. And Lot saw them, and arose to meet them, and bowed with his face to the earth.
verses.19:2: And he said, "Behold now, my lords, please turn aside into the house of your servant and spend the night, and wash your feet; then you may rise early and go on your way." And they said, "No, for we will spend the night in the open square."
verses.19:3: Yet he urged them strongly, so they turned aside to him and came into his house. And he prepared a feast for them and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.
verses.19:4: Before they lay down, the men of the city, the men of Sodom, surrounded the house, from the young even to the old, all the people from every quarter.
verses.19:5: And they called to Lot and said to him, "Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us, that we may know them."
verses.19:6: And Lot went out to them at the doorway, and shut the door behind him.
verses.19:7: And he said, "Please, my brethren, do not act wickedly.
verses.19:8: Behold now, I have two daughters who have not known a man; let me bring them out to you, and do to them as seems good in your eyes; only do nothing to these men, for they have come under the shadow of my roof."
verses.19:9: And they said, "Stand back!" And they said, "This one came to sojourn, and he must continually act as judge! Now we will deal worse with you than with them." So they pressed hard against the man, against Lot, and drew near to break down the door.
verses.19:10: Then the men stretched out their hands and brought Lot to them into the house, and shut the door.
verses.19:11: And they struck the men who were at the doorway of the house with blindness, from the small to the great, so that they wearied themselves trying to find the doorway.
verses.19:12: Then the men said to Lot, "Whom else do you have here? A son-in-law, and your sons, and your daughters, and whoever belongs to you in the city—bring them out of the place!
verses.19:13: For we are about to destroy this place, because the outcry against them has grown great before the LORD, and the LORD has sent us to destroy it."
verses.19:14: So Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law, who were to marry his daughters, and said, "Arise, go out from this place, for the LORD is about to destroy the city!" Yet he seemed as one who was jesting in the eyes of his sons-in-law.
verses.19:15: And when the dawn arose, the angels urged Lot, saying, "Arise, take your wife and your two daughters who are present here, lest you be swept away in the iniquity of the city."
verses.19:16: Yet he lingered; so the men seized his hand, and his wife's hand, and the hands of his two daughters, in the compassion of the LORD upon him; and they brought him out and set him outside the city.
verses.19:17: And it came to pass, when they had brought them outside, that he said, "Escape for your life! Do not look behind you, and do not stay anywhere in all the plain; escape to the mountain, lest you be swept away."
verses.19:18: And Lot said to them, "Oh no, my lords!
verses.19:19: Behold now, your servant has found favor in your sight, and you have magnified your lovingkindness which you have shown to me in preserving my life; yet I cannot escape to the mountain, lest calamity overtake me and I die.
verses.19:20: Behold now, this city is near enough to flee to, and it is a little one; please let me escape there—is it not a little one?—and my soul shall live."
verses.19:21: And he said to him, "Behold, I have granted your request concerning this matter also, that I will not overthrow the city of which you have spoken.
verses.19:22: Make haste, escape there! For I cannot do anything until you arrive there." Therefore the name of the city was called Zoar.
verses.19:23: The sun had risen upon the earth when Lot entered Zoar.
verses.19:24: Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire, from the LORD out of the heavens.
verses.19:25: And He overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and what grew on the ground.
verses.19:26: Yet his wife looked back from behind him, and became a pillar of salt.
verses.19:27: And Abraham rose early in the morning and went to the place where he had stood before the LORD.
verses.19:28: And he looked down toward Sodom and Gomorrah, and toward all the face of the land of the plain; and he looked, and behold, the smoke of the land ascended like the smoke of a furnace.
verses.19:29: And it came to pass, when God destroyed the cities of the plain, that God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out from the midst of the overthrow, when He overthrew the cities in which Lot had dwelt.
verses.19:30: Now Lot went up from Zoar and dwelt in the mountain, and his two daughters were with him, for he feared to dwell in Zoar; and he dwelt in a cave, he and his two daughters.
verses.19:31: And the firstborn said to the younger, "Our father is old, and there is not a man in the earth to come in to us after the manner of all the earth.
verses.19:32: Come, let us make our father drink wine, and let us lie with him, that we may preserve offspring from our father."
verses.19:33: So they made their father drink wine that night; and the firstborn went in and lay with her father, and he did not know when she lay down or when she arose.
verses.19:34: And it came to pass on the next day, that the firstborn said to the younger, "Behold, I lay last night with my father; let us make him drink wine tonight also, and go in and lie with him, that we may preserve offspring from our father."
verses.19:35: So they made their father drink wine that night also; and the younger arose and lay with him, and he did not know when she lay down or when she arose.
verses.19:36: Thus the two daughters of Lot conceived by their father.
verses.19:37: And the firstborn bore a son and called his name Moab; he is the father of Moab to this day.
verses.19:38: And the younger, she also bore a son and called his name Ben-Ammi; he is the father of the sons of Ammon to this day.
verses.20:1: And Abraham journeyed from there toward the land of the Negev, and dwelt between Kadesh and Shur, and sojourned in Gerar.
verses.20:2: And Abraham said concerning Sarah his wife, "She is my sister." So Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took Sarah.
verses.20:3: But God came to Abimelech in a dream by night and said to him, "Behold, you are a dead man because of the woman whom you have taken, for she is a man's wife."
verses.20:4: Now Abimelech had not come near her; and he said, "Lord, will You slay even a righteous nation?
verses.20:5: Did he not say to me, 'She is my sister'? And she, even she herself, said, 'He is my brother.' In the integrity of my heart and the innocence of my hands I have done this."
verses.20:6: And God said to him in the dream, "Yes, I too know that in the integrity of your heart you did this, and I Myself also kept you from sinning against Me; therefore I did not permit you to touch her.
verses.20:7: Now therefore, restore the man's wife, for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you and you shall live. But if you do not restore her, know that you shall surely die, you and all who belong to you."
verses.20:8: So Abimelech rose early in the morning, and called all his servants, and spoke all these words in their hearing; and the men were exceedingly afraid.
verses.20:9: Then Abimelech called Abraham and said to him, "What have you done to us? And how have I sinned against you, that you have brought upon me and upon my kingdom a great sin? You have done deeds to me that ought not to be done."
verses.20:10: And Abimelech said to Abraham, "What did you see, that you have done this thing?"
verses.20:11: And Abraham said, "Because I thought, 'Surely there is no fear of God in this place, and they will slay me on account of my wife.'
verses.20:12: And moreover, indeed she is my sister, the daughter of my father, yet not the daughter of my mother; and she became my wife.
verses.20:13: And it came to pass, when God caused me to wander from my father's house, that I said to her, 'This is the kindness which you shall show to me: at every place where we come, say of me, "He is my brother."'"
verses.20:14: Then Abimelech took flocks and herds, and male and female servants, and gave them to Abraham; and he restored Sarah his wife to him.
verses.20:15: And Abimelech said, "Behold, my land is before you; dwell wherever it seems good in your eyes."
verses.20:16: And to Sarah he said, "Behold, I have given one thousand pieces of silver to your brother; behold, it is a covering of the eyes for you before all who are with you and before all others; thus you are vindicated."
verses.20:17: So Abraham prayed to God; and God healed Abimelech, and his wife, and his maidservants, so that they bore children.
verses.20:18: For the LORD had completely closed every womb of the house of Abimelech, on account of Sarah, Abraham's wife.
verses.21:1: And the LORD visited Sarah just as He had said, and the LORD did for Sarah just as He had spoken.
verses.21:2: So Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the appointed time of which God had spoken to him.
verses.21:3: And Abraham called the name of his son who was born to him, whom Sarah bore to him, Isaac.
verses.21:4: Then Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, just as God had commanded him.
verses.21:5: Now Abraham was one hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.
verses.21:6: And Sarah said, "God has made laughter for me; everyone who hears will laugh with me."
verses.21:7: And she said, "Who would have declared to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne a son in his old age."
verses.21:8: And the child grew and was weaned. And Abraham made a great feast on the day that Isaac was weaned.
verses.21:9: Now Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, mocking.
verses.21:10: Therefore she said to Abraham, "Drive out this maidservant and her son; for the son of this maidservant shall not be heir with my son, with Isaac."
verses.21:11: And the matter was exceedingly grievous in the sight of Abraham on account of his son.
verses.21:12: But God said to Abraham, "Do not let it be grievous in your sight because of the lad and because of your maidservant. In all that Sarah says to you, heed her voice; for in Isaac your seed shall be named.
verses.21:13: Yet of the son of the maidservant I will also make a nation, because he is your seed."
verses.21:14: So Abraham rose early in the morning, and took bread and a skin of water, and gave them to Hagar, putting them on her shoulder, together with the child, and sent her away. Then she departed and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.
verses.21:15: And when the water in the skin was spent, she laid the child under one of the shrubs.
verses.21:16: Then she went and sat down opposite him at a distance, about a bowshot away; for she said, "Do not let me look upon the death of the child." So she sat opposite him, and lifted up her voice and wept.
verses.21:17: And God heard the voice of the lad. Then the Angel of God called to Hagar out of heaven and said to her, "What ails you, Hagar? Do not fear, for God has heard the voice of the lad where he is.
verses.21:18: Arise, lift up the lad and hold him firmly with your hand, for I will make him a great nation."
verses.21:19: Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. And she went and filled the skin with water, and gave the lad a drink.
verses.21:20: And God was with the lad, and he grew; and he dwelt in the wilderness and became an archer.
verses.21:21: He dwelt in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
verses.21:22: Now it came to pass at that time that Abimelech and Phichol, the commander of his army, spoke to Abraham, saying, "God is with you in all that you do.
verses.21:23: Now therefore, swear to me here by God that you will not deal falsely with me, nor with my offspring, nor with my posterity; but according to the kindness that I have shown to you, so you shall do to me and to the land in which you have sojourned."
verses.21:25: Then Abraham reproved Abimelech on account of a well of water which Abimelech's servants had seized.
verses.21:26: And Abimelech said, "I do not know who has done this thing; neither did you tell me, nor have I heard of it until today."
verses.21:27: So Abraham took sheep and oxen and gave them to Abimelech, and the two of them made a covenant.
verses.21:28: And Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock by themselves.
verses.21:29: Then Abimelech said to Abraham, "What is the meaning of these seven ewe lambs which you have set by themselves?"
verses.21:30: And he said, "You shall receive the seven ewe lambs from my hand, that it may be a witness for me that I have dug this well."
verses.21:31: Therefore he called that place Beersheba, because there the two of them swore an oath.
verses.21:32: Thus they made a covenant at Beersheba. Then Abimelech rose up, along with Phichol the commander of his army, and they returned to the land of the Philistines.
verses.21:33: And Abraham planted a tamarisk tree at Beersheba, and there he called upon the name of the LORD, the Everlasting God.
verses.21:34: And Abraham sojourned in the land of the Philistines many days.
verses.22:1: Now it came to pass after these things that God tested Abraham, and said to him, "Abraham!" And he said, "Here I am."
verses.22:2: Then He said, "Take now your son, your only one whom you love—Isaac—and go to the land of Moriah, and offer him there as a burnt offering upon one of the mountains of which I shall tell you."
verses.22:3: So Abraham rose early in the morning and saddled his donkey, and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son; and he split the wood for the burnt offering, and arose and went to the place of which God had told him.
verses.22:4: On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes and saw the place from afar.
verses.22:5: And Abraham said to his young men, "Remain here with the donkey, while the lad and I go over there; we will worship, and we will return to you."
verses.22:6: So Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering and laid it upon Isaac his son; and he took in his hand the fire and the knife, and the two of them went on together.
verses.22:7: Then Isaac spoke to Abraham his father and said, "My father!" And he said, "Here I am, my son." Then he said, "Behold, the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?"
verses.22:8: And Abraham said, "God will provide for Himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son." So the two of them went on together.
verses.22:9: Then they came to the place of which God had told him. And Abraham built the altar there and arranged the wood in order; and he bound Isaac his son and laid him upon the altar, on top of the wood.
verses.22:10: And Abraham stretched out his hand and took the knife to slay his son.
verses.22:11: But the Angel of the LORD called to him out of heaven and said, "Abraham, Abraham!" And he said, "Here I am."
verses.22:12: And He said, "Do not lay your hand upon the lad, nor do anything to him; for now I know that you fear God, seeing you have not withheld your son, your only one, from Me."
verses.22:13: Then Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, behind him was a ram caught in a thicket by its horns. So Abraham went and took the ram, and offered it up for a burnt offering in place of his son.
verses.22:14: And Abraham called the name of that place The LORD Will Provide; as it is said to this day, "On the mountain of the LORD it shall be provided."
verses.22:15: Then the Angel of the LORD called to Abraham a second time out of heaven,
verses.22:16: and said, "By Myself I have sworn, declares the LORD, because you have done this thing, and have not withheld your son, your only one,
verses.22:17: I will surely bless you, and I will surely multiply your seed as the stars of heaven and as the sand upon the seashore; and your seed shall possess the gate of his enemies.
verses.22:18: And in your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed, because you have obeyed My voice."
verses.22:19: So Abraham returned to his young men, and they arose and went together to Beersheba; and Abraham dwelt at Beersheba.
verses.22:20: Now it came to pass after these things that it was told to Abraham, saying, "Behold, Milcah also has borne children to your brother Nahor:
verses.22:21: Uz his firstborn, Buz his brother, Kemuel the father of Aram,
verses.22:22: Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel."
verses.22:23: And Bethuel fathered Rebekah. These eight Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham's brother.
verses.22:24: And his concubine, whose name was Reumah, also bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
verses.23:1: Now the life of Sarah was one hundred and twenty-seven years—the years of Sarah's life.
verses.23:2: And Sarah died in Kiriath Arba, that is, Hebron, in the land of Canaan; and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah and to weep over her.
verses.23:3: Then Abraham rose up from before his dead and spoke to the sons of Heth, saying,
verses.23:4: "I am a foreigner and a sojourner among you; grant me a burial possession among you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight."
verses.23:5: And the sons of Heth answered Abraham, saying to him,
