verses.23:6: "Hear us, my lord: you are a prince of God in our midst. In the choicest of our tombs bury your dead; none of us will withhold his tomb from you to keep you from burying your dead."
verses.23:7: Then Abraham stood up and bowed down to the people of the land, to the sons of Heth.
verses.23:8: And he spoke with them, saying, "If it is indeed your desire that I bury my dead out of my sight, hear me, and intercede for me with Ephron the son of Zohar,
verses.23:9: that he may give me the cave of Machpelah, which belongs to him, which lies at the edge of his field. For its full price let him grant it to me in your midst as a burial possession."
verses.23:10: Now Ephron was sitting among the sons of Heth; and Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the hearing of the sons of Heth, before all who entered the gate of his city, saying,
verses.23:11: "No, my lord, hear me: I give you the field, and the cave that is in it I also give to you; in the presence of the sons of my people I give it to you. Bury your dead."
verses.23:12: Then Abraham bowed down before the people of the land.
verses.23:13: And he spoke to Ephron in the hearing of the people of the land, saying, "If you will only hear me: I give the price of the field; accept it from me, that I may bury my dead there."
verses.23:14: And Ephron answered Abraham, saying to him,
verses.23:15: "My lord, hear me: a piece of land worth four hundred shekels of silver—what is that between me and you? Therefore bury your dead."
verses.23:16: So Abraham listened to Ephron, and Abraham weighed out for Ephron the silver that he had named in the hearing of the sons of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, current among the merchants.
verses.23:17: Thus the field of Ephron in Machpelah, which was before Mamre—the field and the cave that was in it, and all the trees that were in the field within all its borders all around—was confirmed
verses.23:18: to Abraham as a purchased possession in the sight of the sons of Heth, in the presence of all who entered the gate of his city.
verses.23:19: And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah, facing Mamre, that is, Hebron, in the land of Canaan.
verses.23:20: So the field and the cave that is in it were confirmed to Abraham as a burial possession by the sons of Heth.
verses.24:1: Now Abraham was old, advanced in days; and the LORD had blessed Abraham in everything.
verses.24:2: And Abraham said to his servant, the elder of his house, who ruled over all that belonged to him, "Please place your hand under my thigh,
verses.24:3: and I will have you swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of the earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose midst I dwell;
verses.24:4: but you shall go to my land and to my kindred, and take a wife for my son Isaac."
verses.24:5: And the servant said to him, "Perhaps the woman will not be willing to follow me to this land. Must I indeed bring your son back to the land from which you came out?"
verses.24:6: And Abraham said to him, "Take heed to yourself, lest you bring my son back there.
verses.24:7: The LORD, the God of heaven, who took me from my father's house and from the land of my kindred, and who spoke to me and swore to me, saying, 'To your seed I will give this land,' He will send His angel before you, and you shall take a wife for my son from there.
verses.24:8: And if the woman is not willing to follow you, then you shall be clear of this oath of mine; only you shall not bring my son back there."
verses.24:9: So the servant placed his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and swore to him concerning this matter.
verses.24:10: Then the servant took ten camels from his master's camels and departed, and all the good things of his master were in his hand; and he arose and journeyed to Aram Naharaim, to the city of Nahor.
verses.24:11: And he made the camels kneel down outside the city by the well of water at the time of evening, the time when the women go out to draw water.
verses.24:12: And he said, "O LORD, God of my master Abraham, please grant me success today, and show lovingkindness to my master Abraham.
verses.24:13: Behold, I am standing by the spring of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.
verses.24:14: Now let it come to pass that the maiden to whom I say, 'Please lower your pitcher that I may drink,' and she says, 'Drink, and I will give your camels water as well'—let her be the one You have appointed for Your servant Isaac; and by this I shall know that You have shown lovingkindness to my master."
verses.24:15: And it came to pass, before he had finished speaking, that behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother, with her pitcher upon her shoulder.
verses.24:16: Now the maiden was exceedingly fair to look upon, a virgin, and no man had known her. And she went down to the spring, filled her pitcher, and came up.
verses.24:17: And the servant ran to meet her and said, "Please let me sip a little water from your pitcher."
verses.24:18: And she said, "Drink, my lord." Then she quickly lowered her pitcher upon her hand and gave him a drink.
verses.24:19: And when she had finished giving him a drink, she said, "For your camels also I will draw water, until they have finished drinking."
verses.24:20: So she hastened and emptied her pitcher into the trough, and ran again to the well to draw water, and drew for all his camels.
verses.24:21: And the man gazed upon her in wonder, keeping silent to know whether the LORD had made his journey prosperous or not.
verses.24:22: And it came to pass, when the camels had finished drinking, that the man took a gold nose ring weighing half a shekel, and two bracelets for her wrists weighing ten shekels of gold.
verses.24:23: And he said, "Whose daughter are you? Please tell me, is there room in your father's house for us to lodge?"
verses.24:24: And she said to him, "I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor."
verses.24:25: Moreover she said to him, "We have both straw and fodder in abundance, and room to lodge as well."
verses.24:26: Then the man bowed his head and worshiped the LORD.
verses.24:27: And he said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not forsaken His lovingkindness and His truth toward my master. As for me, while I was on the way, the LORD led me to the house of my master's brethren."
verses.24:28: So the maiden ran and told her mother's household concerning these things.
verses.24:29: Now Rebekah had a brother whose name was Laban, and Laban ran outside to the man, to the spring.
verses.24:30: And it came to pass, when he saw the nose ring and the bracelets upon his sister's wrists, and when he heard the words of his sister Rebekah, saying, "Thus the man spoke to me," that he came to the man; and behold, he was standing by the camels at the spring.
verses.24:31: And he said, "Come in, O blessed of the LORD! Why do you stand outside? For I have prepared the house, and a place for the camels."
verses.24:32: So the man came into the house. And he unloaded the camels, and provided straw and fodder for the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.
verses.24:33: Then food was set before him to eat, but he said, "I will not eat until I have spoken my words." And he said, "Speak on."
verses.24:34: And he said, "I am Abraham's servant.
verses.24:35: And the LORD has blessed my master exceedingly, and he has become great; and He has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, menservants and maidservants, and camels and donkeys.
verses.24:36: And Sarah my master's wife bore a son to my master after she had grown old, and he has given to him all that he possesses.
verses.24:37: Now my master made me swear, saying, 'You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I dwell;
verses.24:38: but you shall go to my father's house and to my family, and take a wife for my son.'
verses.24:39: And I said to my master, 'Perhaps the woman will not follow me.'
verses.24:40: And he said to me, 'The LORD, before whom I walk, will send His angel with you and prosper your way; and you shall take a wife for my son from my family and from my father's house.
verses.24:41: Then you shall be clear of my oath when you come to my family; and if they do not give her to you, then you shall be free from my oath.'
verses.24:42: And I came today to the spring and said, 'O LORD, God of my master Abraham, if You will indeed prosper the way upon which I go,
verses.24:43: behold, I am standing by the spring of water; and let it come to pass that the young woman who comes out to draw water, to whom I say, "Please give me a little water from your pitcher to drink,"
verses.24:44: and she says to me, "Drink yourself, and I will draw for your camels also"—let her be the woman whom the LORD has appointed for my master's son.'
verses.24:45: Before I had finished speaking in my heart, behold, Rebekah came out with her pitcher upon her shoulder, and she went down to the spring and drew water. And I said to her, 'Please give me a drink.'
verses.24:46: And she quickly lowered her pitcher from her shoulder and said, 'Drink, and I will give your camels water as well.' So I drank, and she watered the camels also.
verses.24:47: Then I asked her and said, 'Whose daughter are you?' And she said, 'The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor's son, whom Milcah bore to him.' So I placed the nose ring on her nose and the bracelets upon her wrists.
verses.24:48: And I bowed my head and worshiped the LORD, and blessed the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me in the way of truth to take the daughter of my master's brother for his son.
verses.24:49: Now therefore, if you will show lovingkindness and truth to my master, tell me; and if not, tell me, that I may turn to the right or to the left."
verses.24:50: Then Laban and Bethuel answered and said, "This matter has come forth from the LORD; we cannot speak to you either bad or good.
verses.24:51: Behold, Rebekah is before you; take her and go, and let her become the wife of your master's son, as the LORD has spoken."
verses.24:52: And it came to pass, when Abraham's servant heard their words, that he bowed down to the earth before the LORD.
verses.24:53: Then the servant brought forth ornaments of silver, ornaments of gold, and garments, and gave them to Rebekah; he also gave precious gifts to her brother and to her mother.
verses.24:54: And they ate and drank, he and the men who were with him, and lodged the night. And they arose in the morning, and he said, "Send me away to my master."
verses.24:55: But her brother and her mother said, "Let the maiden abide with us a few days, at least ten; afterward she may go."
verses.24:56: And he said to them, "Do not delay me, seeing that the LORD has prospered my way; send me away, that I may go to my master."
verses.24:57: So they said, "Let us call the maiden and ask her directly."
verses.24:58: Then they called Rebekah and said to her, "Will you go with this man?" And she said, "I will go."
verses.24:59: So they sent away Rebekah their sister and her nurse, and Abraham's servant and his men.
verses.24:60: And they blessed Rebekah and said to her, "Our sister, may you become thousands of ten thousands! And may your seed possess the gate of those who hate them!"
verses.24:61: Then Rebekah and her maidens arose, and rode upon the camels, and followed the man. So the servant took Rebekah and departed.
verses.24:62: Now Isaac had come from the way of Beer Lahai Roi, for he was dwelling in the land of the Negev.
verses.24:63: And Isaac went out to meditate in the field toward evening; and he lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, camels were approaching.
verses.24:64: And Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Isaac, she alighted from the camel.
verses.24:65: And she said to the servant, "Who is this man walking in the field to meet us?" And the servant said, "He is my master." So she took her veil and covered herself.
verses.24:66: And the servant recounted to Isaac all the things that he had done.
verses.24:67: Then Isaac brought her into the tent of his mother Sarah; and he took Rebekah, and she became his wife, and he loved her. So Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.
verses.25:1: And Abraham again took a wife, and her name was Keturah.
verses.25:2: And she bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
verses.25:3: Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan. And the sons of Dedan were the Asshurim, the Letushim, and the Leummim.
verses.25:4: And the sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the sons of Keturah.
verses.25:5: Now Abraham gave all that belonged to him to Isaac.
verses.25:6: But to the sons of the concubines whom Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts; and while he was still living, he sent them away from Isaac his son, eastward to the land of the east.
verses.25:7: These are the days of the years of Abraham's life which he lived: one hundred seventy-five years.
verses.25:8: Then Abraham breathed his last and died in a good old age, an old man and full of years, and was gathered to his people.
verses.25:9: And his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, which lies before Mamre.
verses.25:10: The field which Abraham purchased from the sons of Heth—there Abraham was buried, and Sarah his wife.
verses.25:11: And it came to pass after the death of Abraham that God blessed Isaac his son; and Isaac dwelt by Beer Lahai Roi.
verses.25:12: Now these are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's maidservant, bore to Abraham.
verses.25:13: And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names according to their generations: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebajoth; then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
verses.25:15: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
verses.25:16: These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names by their villages and by their encampments—twelve princes according to their tribes.
verses.25:17: And these were the years of the life of Ishmael: one hundred thirty-seven years; and he breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people.
verses.25:18: They dwelt from Havilah as far as Shur, which lies east of Egypt as one goes toward Assyria; he settled over against all his brethren.
verses.25:19: Now these are the generations of Isaac, Abraham's son: Abraham fathered Isaac.
verses.25:20: Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean of Paddan Aram, the sister of Laban the Aramean, to be his wife.
verses.25:21: And Isaac pleaded with the LORD on behalf of his wife, because she was barren; and the LORD granted his plea, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
verses.25:22: But the children struggled together within her, and she said, "If it is so, why am I thus?" So she went to inquire of the LORD.
verses.25:23: And the LORD said to her, "Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples shall be separated from your body; one people shall be stronger than the other, and the older shall serve the younger."
verses.25:24: When her days to give birth were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb.
verses.25:25: And the first came forth red, all over like a hairy garment; so they called his name Esau.
verses.25:26: Afterward his brother came forth, and his hand grasped Esau's heel; so his name was called Jacob. And Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them.
verses.25:27: So the boys grew; and Esau became a skillful hunter, a man of the field, while Jacob was a quiet man, dwelling in tents.
verses.25:28: And Isaac loved Esau because he had a taste for wild game, but Rebekah loved Jacob.
verses.25:29: Now Jacob was boiling a stew; and Esau came in from the field, and he was weary.
verses.25:30: And Esau said to Jacob, "Please let me eat some of that red—that red stew—for I am weary." Therefore his name was called Edom.
verses.25:31: And Jacob said, "Sell me your birthright this very day."
verses.25:32: And Esau said, "Behold, I am about to die; so of what use is a birthright to me?"
verses.25:33: Then Jacob said, "Swear to me this very day." So he swore to him, and sold his birthright to Jacob.
verses.25:34: And Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew; and he ate and drank, arose and went his way. Thus Esau despised the birthright.
verses.26:1: Now there was a famine in the land, besides the first famine that was in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines, in Gerar.
verses.26:2: Then the LORD appeared to him and said, "Do not go down to Egypt; dwell in the land of which I shall tell you.
verses.26:3: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and bless you; for to you and to your seed I will give all these lands, and I will establish the oath which I swore to Abraham your father.
verses.26:4: And I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven, and I will give to your seed all these lands; and in your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed,
verses.26:5: because Abraham obeyed My voice and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes, and My laws."
verses.26:7: And the men of the place asked about his wife, and he said, "She is my sister"; for he feared to say, "She is my wife," thinking, "Lest the men of the place slay me on account of Rebekah, because she is fair to look upon."
verses.26:8: Now it came to pass, when his days there had grown long, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out through a window and saw, and behold, Isaac was caressing Rebekah his wife.
verses.26:9: Then Abimelech summoned Isaac and said, "Surely, behold, she is your wife! How then did you say, 'She is my sister'?" And Isaac said to him, "Because I said, 'Lest I die on account of her.'"
verses.26:10: And Abimelech said, "What is this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have lain with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us."
verses.26:11: So Abimelech charged all the people, saying, "Whoever touches this man or his wife shall surely be put to death."
verses.26:12: Then Isaac sowed in that land, and reaped in that same year a hundredfold; and the LORD blessed him.
verses.26:13: And the man became great, and continued to grow greater until he became exceedingly great.
verses.26:14: For he had possessions of flocks and possessions of herds and a great household of servants, so that the Philistines envied him.
verses.26:15: Now all the wells which his father's servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines had stopped up and filled with earth.
verses.26:16: And Abimelech said to Isaac, "Depart from us, for you have become far mightier than we."
verses.26:17: So Isaac departed from there, and pitched his tent in the Valley of Gerar, and dwelt there.
verses.26:18: And Isaac dug again the wells of water which they had dug in the days of Abraham his father, for the Philistines had stopped them up after the death of Abraham; and he called them by the same names which his father had called them.
verses.26:19: Also Isaac's servants dug in the valley, and found there a well of living water.
verses.26:20: But the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac's herdsmen, saying, "The water is ours." So he called the name of the well Esek, because they contended with him.
verses.26:21: Then they dug another well, and they quarreled over that one also; so he called its name Sitnah.
verses.26:22: And he moved from there and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it; so he called its name Rehoboth, and said, "For now the LORD has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land."
verses.26:23: Then he went up from there to Beersheba.
verses.26:24: And the LORD appeared to him the same night and said, "I am the God of Abraham your father; do not fear, for I am with you. I will bless you and multiply your seed for the sake of My servant Abraham."
verses.26:25: So he built an altar there and called on the name of the LORD, and pitched his tent there; and there Isaac's servants dug a well.
verses.26:26: Then Abimelech came to him from Gerar with Ahuzzath his friend, and Phichol the commander of his army.
verses.26:27: And Isaac said to them, "Why have you come to me, seeing that you hate me and have sent me away from you?"
verses.26:28: And they said, "We have clearly seen that the LORD has been with you. So we said, 'Let there now be an oath between us, between us and you, and let us make a covenant with you,
verses.26:29: that you will do us no harm, just as we have not touched you, and just as we have done to you nothing but good and sent you away in peace.' You are now the blessed of the LORD."
verses.26:30: So he made them a feast, and they ate and drank.
verses.26:31: And they rose early in the morning and swore an oath one to another; then Isaac sent them on their way, and they departed from him in peace.
verses.26:32: Now it came to pass on that same day that Isaac's servants came and told him about the well which they had dug, and said to him, "We have found water."
verses.26:33: So he called it Shibah. Therefore the name of the city is Beersheba to this day.
verses.26:34: When Esau was forty years old, he took as wives Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite.
verses.26:35: And they were a bitterness of spirit to Isaac and Rebekah.
verses.27:1: Now it came to pass, when Isaac had grown old and his eyes were too dim to see, that he called Esau his elder son and said to him, "My son." And he said to him, "Here I am."
verses.27:2: Then he said, "Behold now, I have grown old; I do not know the day of my death.
verses.27:3: Now therefore, take your weapons, your quiver and your bow, and go out into the field and hunt wild game for me.
verses.27:4: And prepare savory food for me, such as I love, and bring it to me that I may eat, so that my soul may bless you before I die."
verses.27:5: Now Rebekah was listening as Isaac spoke to Esau his son. And Esau went into the field to hunt wild game to bring back.
verses.27:6: Then Rebekah spoke to Jacob her son, saying, "Behold, I heard your father speaking to Esau your brother, saying,
verses.27:7: 'Bring me wild game and prepare savory food for me, that I may eat and bless you in the presence of the LORD before my death.'
verses.27:8: Now therefore, my son, heed my voice in what I command you.
verses.27:9: Go now to the flock and fetch for me from there two choice young goats, and I will prepare savory food from them for your father, such as he loves.
verses.27:10: Then you shall bring it to your father so that he may eat, in order that he may bless you before his death."
verses.27:11: And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, "Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, whereas I am a smooth-skinned man.
verses.27:12: Perhaps my father will feel me, and I shall appear in his eyes as a deceiver; and I shall bring a curse upon myself and not a blessing."
verses.27:13: But his mother said to him, "Let your curse be upon me, my son; only heed my voice, and go, fetch them for me."
verses.27:14: So he went and fetched them and brought them to his mother, and his mother prepared savory food, such as his father loved.
verses.27:15: Then Rebekah took the finest garments of Esau her elder son, which were with her in the house, and put them on Jacob her younger son.
verses.27:16: And she placed the skins of the young goats upon his hands and upon the smooth part of his neck.
verses.27:17: Then she put the savory food and the bread, which she had prepared, into the hand of Jacob her son.
verses.27:18: So he went in to his father and said, "My father." And he said, "Here I am. Who are you, my son?"
verses.27:19: And Jacob said to his father, "I am Esau your firstborn; I have done just as you told me. Arise, I pray, sit up and eat of my wild game, so that your soul may bless me."
verses.27:20: But Isaac said to his son, "How is it that you have found it so quickly, my son?" And he said, "Because the LORD your God brought it before me."
verses.27:21: Then Isaac said to Jacob, "Draw near, I pray, that I may feel you, my son, whether you are indeed my son Esau or not."
verses.27:22: So Jacob drew near to Isaac his father, and he felt him and said, "The voice is the voice of Jacob, yet the hands are the hands of Esau."
verses.27:23: And he did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like the hands of his brother Esau; so he blessed him.
verses.27:24: Then he said, "Are you truly my son Esau?" And he said, "I am."
verses.27:25: He said, "Bring it near to me, and I will eat of my son's wild game, so that my soul may bless you." So he brought it near to him, and he ate; and he brought him wine, and he drank.
verses.27:26: Then Isaac his father said to him, "Draw near now and kiss me, my son."
verses.27:27: So he drew near and kissed him; and he smelled the fragrance of his garments and blessed him, and said, "See, the fragrance of my son is like the fragrance of a field which the LORD has blessed.
verses.27:28: May God grant you of the dew of heaven, and of the richness of the earth, and an abundance of grain and new wine.
verses.27:29: Let peoples serve you, and nations bow down to you; be master over your brethren, and let your mother's sons bow down to you. Cursed be everyone who curses you, and blessed be everyone who blesses you."
verses.27:30: Now it came to pass, as soon as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob, and Jacob had scarcely gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting.
verses.27:31: He also had prepared savory food and brought it to his father, and he said to his father, "Let my father arise and eat of his son's wild game, so that your soul may bless me."
verses.27:32: And Isaac his father said to him, "Who are you?" And he said, "I am your son, your firstborn, Esau."
verses.27:33: Then Isaac trembled with an exceedingly great trembling and said, "Who then was he who hunted wild game and brought it to me? I ate of it all before you came, and I have blessed him—and indeed he shall be blessed."
verses.27:34: When Esau heard the words of his father, he cried out with an exceedingly great and bitter cry, and said to his father, "Bless me, even me also, O my father!"
verses.27:35: And he said, "Your brother came deceitfully and has taken your blessing."
verses.27:36: And he said, "Is he not rightly named Jacob? For he has supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright, and behold, now he has taken away my blessing." And he said, "Have you not reserved a blessing for me?"
verses.27:37: Then Isaac answered and said to Esau, "Behold, I have appointed him master over you, and all his brethren I have given to him as servants; and with grain and new wine I have sustained him. What then can I do for you, my son?"
verses.27:38: Then Esau said to his father, "Do you have only one blessing, my father? Bless me, me also, my father!" And Esau raised his voice and wept.
verses.27:39: Then Isaac his father answered and said to him, "Behold, your dwelling shall be of the richness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above.
verses.27:40: By your sword you shall live, and you shall serve your brother; yet it shall come to pass, when you grow restless, that you shall break his yoke from off your neck."
verses.27:41: So Esau bore hatred against Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him, and Esau said in his heart, "The days of mourning for my father are drawing near; then I will slay my brother Jacob."
verses.27:42: Now the words of Esau her elder son were told to Rebekah. So she sent and called Jacob her younger son, and said to him, "Behold, your brother Esau comforts himself concerning you by intending to slay you.
verses.27:43: Now therefore, my son, heed my voice: arise and flee to my brother Laban in Haran,
verses.27:44: and dwell with him a few days, until your brother's fury turns away,
verses.27:45: until your brother's wrath turns away from you and he forgets what you have done to him; then I will send and bring you back from there. Why should I be bereaved of you both in one day?"
verses.27:46: Then Rebekah said to Isaac, "I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife from the daughters of Heth, like these who are of the daughters of the land, what good will my life be to me?"
verses.28:1: Then Isaac called Jacob and blessed him, and charged him and said to him, "You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.
verses.28:2: Arise, go to Padan Aram, to the house of Bethuel your mother's father, and take for yourself a wife from there, from the daughters of Laban your mother's brother.
verses.28:3: May God Almighty bless you, and make you fruitful and multiply you, that you may become an assembly of peoples.
verses.28:4: And may He give you the blessing of Abraham, to you and to your descendants with you, that you may inherit the land of your sojournings, which God gave to Abraham."
verses.28:5: So Isaac sent Jacob away, and he went to Padan Aram, to Laban the son of Bethuel the Aramean, the brother of Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.
verses.28:6: Now Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him away to Padan Aram to take a wife for himself from there, and that as he blessed him he charged him, saying, "You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan."
verses.28:7: And Jacob had obeyed his father and his mother and had gone to Padan Aram.
verses.28:8: Also Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan were displeasing in the eyes of Isaac his father.
verses.28:9: So Esau went to Ishmael and took Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham's son, the sister of Nebaioth, to be his wife in addition to the wives he already had.
verses.28:10: Now Jacob departed from Beersheba and went toward Haran.
verses.28:11: So he came upon a certain place and stayed the night there, because the sun had set. And he took one of the stones of that place and set it at his head, and he lay down in that place.
verses.28:12: Then he dreamed, and behold, a ladder was set up on the earth, and its top reached into heaven; and behold, the angels of God were ascending and descending upon it.
verses.28:13: And behold, the LORD stood above it and said, "I am the LORD, the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac. The land on which you lie I will give to you and to your descendants.
verses.28:14: Also your descendants shall be as the dust of the earth; you shall spread abroad to the west and to the east, to the north and to the south; and in you and in your descendants all the families of the earth shall be blessed.
verses.28:15: Behold, I am with you and will keep you wherever you go, and will bring you back to this land; for I will not forsake you until I have accomplished what I have spoken to you."
verses.28:16: And Jacob awoke from his sleep and said, "Truly the LORD is in this place, and I myself did not know it."
verses.28:17: And he feared and said, "How awe-inspiring is this place! This is nothing other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven."
verses.28:18: Then Jacob rose early in the morning, and took the stone that he had set at his head, and set it up as a pillar, and poured oil on top of it.
verses.28:19: And he called the name of that place Bethel; however, the name of that city had formerly been Luz.
verses.28:20: Then Jacob vowed a vow, saying, "If God will be with me, and will watch over me on this journey that I am taking, and will give me bread to eat and clothing to put on,
verses.28:21: and I return in peace to my father's house, then the LORD shall be my God.
verses.28:22: And this stone, which I have set as a pillar, shall be a house of God, and of everything that You give me I will surely give a tenth to You."
verses.29:1: Then Jacob lifted up his feet and went to the land of the sons of the East.
verses.29:2: And he looked, and behold, a well was in the field; and behold, three flocks of sheep were lying there beside it, for from that well they watered the flocks, and the stone upon the mouth of the well was great.
verses.29:3: Now all the flocks would be gathered there, and they would roll the stone from the mouth of the well and water the sheep, and restore the stone to its place upon the mouth of the well.
verses.29:4: And Jacob said to them, "My brethren, from where are you?" And they replied, "We are from Haran."
verses.29:5: Then he asked them, "Do you know Laban the son of Nahor?" And they said, "We know him."
verses.29:6: And he said to them, "Is it well with him?" And they answered, "It is well; and behold, Rachel his daughter is coming with the sheep."
verses.29:7: Then he said, "Behold, it is still high day; it is not the time for the livestock to be gathered. Water the sheep, and go and pasture them."
verses.29:8: But they replied, "We cannot, until all the flocks are gathered together and they roll the stone from the mouth of the well; then we will water the sheep."
verses.29:9: While he was still speaking with them, Rachel came with the sheep of her father, for she was a shepherdess.
verses.29:10: And it came to pass, when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother's brother, that Jacob drew near and rolled the stone from the mouth of the well, and watered the sheep of Laban his mother's brother.
verses.29:11: Then Jacob kissed Rachel, and he raised his voice and wept.
verses.29:12: And Jacob declared to Rachel that he was her father's kinsman, and that he was the son of Rebekah; and she ran and told her father.
verses.29:13: And it came to pass, when Laban heard the tidings concerning Jacob his sister's son, that he ran to meet him, embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him into his house. And he recounted to Laban all these things.
verses.29:14: And Laban said to him, "Truly, you are my bone and my flesh!" So he dwelt with him for a full month.
verses.29:15: Then Laban said to Jacob, "Just because you are my kinsman, should you serve me for nothing? Tell me, what shall your wages be?"
verses.29:16: Now Laban had two daughters: the elder's name was Leah, and the younger's name was Rachel.
verses.29:17: Leah's eyes were tender, while Rachel was lovely in form and lovely in appearance.
verses.29:18: And Jacob loved Rachel; therefore he said, "I will serve you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel."
verses.29:19: And Laban replied, "It is better for me to give her to you than to give her to another man; abide with me."
verses.29:20: Thus Jacob served seven years for Rachel, yet in his eyes they were like only a few days because of his love for her.
verses.29:21: Then Jacob spoke to Laban, "Give me my wife, for my days are completed, so that I may go in to her."
verses.29:22: So Laban assembled all the men of the place and held a feast.
verses.29:23: And when evening came, he took his daughter Leah and brought her to Jacob; and he went in to her.
verses.29:24: Moreover, Laban gave Zilpah his maidservant to Leah his daughter as her maidservant.
verses.29:25: And when morning came, behold, it was Leah! And he said to Laban, "What is this that you have done to me? Did I not serve with you for Rachel? Why then have you deceived me?"
verses.29:26: And Laban answered, "It is not done thus in our place, to give the younger before the firstborn.
verses.29:27: Complete the week of this one, and we will give you this other one also, in return for the service that you shall serve with me seven more years."
verses.29:28: And Jacob did so, and completed her week; then Laban gave him Rachel his daughter to be his wife.
verses.29:29: And Laban gave Bilhah his maidservant to Rachel his daughter as her maidservant.
verses.29:30: So he went in to Rachel also, and indeed he loved Rachel more than Leah; and he served with him seven more years.
verses.29:31: And the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, and He opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.
verses.29:32: And Leah conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Reuben; for she said, "Because the LORD has looked upon my affliction; surely now my husband will love me."
verses.29:33: And she conceived again and bore a son, and she said, "Because the LORD has heard that I am unloved, He has given me this one also." So she named him Simeon.
verses.29:34: And she conceived yet again and bore a son, and she said, "Now this time my husband will be joined to me, for I have borne him three sons." Therefore his name was called Levi.
verses.29:35: And she conceived again and bore a son, and she said, "This time I will praise the LORD." Therefore she named him Judah; and she ceased bearing.
verses.30:1: And Rachel saw that she bore no children to Jacob, so Rachel grew envious of her sister and said to Jacob, "Give me children, or else I will die!"
verses.30:2: Then the anger of Jacob was kindled against Rachel, and he said, "Am I in God's place, who has withheld the fruit of the womb from you?"
verses.30:3: And she said, "Behold, my maidservant Bilhah! Go in to her, that she may bear upon my knees, and that I also may be built up through her."
verses.30:4: So she gave him Bilhah her handmaid as a wife, and Jacob went in to her.
verses.30:5: And Bilhah conceived and bore a son to Jacob.
verses.30:6: Then Rachel said, "God has vindicated me, and He has also heard my voice and given me a son." Therefore she called his name Dan.
verses.30:7: And Bilhah, Rachel's handmaid, conceived again and bore a second son to Jacob.
verses.30:8: And Rachel said, "With fierce wrestlings I have wrestled with my sister, and I have also prevailed." So she called his name Naphtali.
verses.30:9: When Leah saw that she had ceased from bearing, she took Zilpah her handmaid and gave her to Jacob as a wife.
verses.30:10: And Zilpah, Leah's handmaid, bore a son to Jacob.
verses.30:11: Then Leah said, "Good fortune has come!" So she called his name Gad.
verses.30:12: And Zilpah, Leah's handmaid, bore a second son to Jacob.
verses.30:13: Then Leah said, "What happiness is mine! For the daughters will call me blessed." So she called his name Asher.
verses.30:14: Now Reuben went out in the days of the wheat harvest and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them to Leah his mother. Then Rachel said to Leah, "Please give me some of your son's mandrakes."
verses.30:15: But she said to her, "Is it too small a thing that you have taken my husband, that you would also take my son's mandrakes?" And Rachel said, "Therefore he shall lie with you tonight in exchange for your son's mandrakes."
verses.30:16: When Jacob came in from the field in the evening, Leah went out to meet him and said, "You must come in to me, for I have surely hired you with my son's mandrakes." So he lay with her that night.
verses.30:17: And God heard Leah, and she conceived and bore a fifth son to Jacob.
verses.30:18: Then Leah said, "God has given me my reward, because I gave my handmaid to my husband." So she called his name Issachar.
verses.30:19: And Leah conceived again and bore a sixth son to Jacob.
verses.30:20: And Leah said, "God has endowed me with a good gift; this time my husband will dwell with me, for I have borne him six sons." So she called his name Zebulun.
verses.30:21: Afterward she bore a daughter, and called her name Dinah.
verses.30:22: Then God remembered Rachel, and God heard her and opened her womb.
verses.30:23: And she conceived and bore a son, and said, "God has taken away my reproach."
verses.30:24: So she called his name Joseph, saying, "May the LORD add to me another son."
verses.30:25: And it came to pass, when Rachel had borne Joseph, that Jacob said to Laban, "Send me away, that I may go to my own place and to my own land.
verses.30:26: Give me my wives and my children for whom I have served you, and let me depart; for you know the service with which I have served you."
verses.30:27: And Laban said to him, "If now I have found favor in your sight—I have learned by divination that the LORD has blessed me because of you."
verses.30:28: And he said, "Name your wages to me, and I will pay them."
verses.30:29: So he said to him, "You know how I have served you, and how your livestock has fared with me.
verses.30:30: For what you had before my coming was little, and it has increased into a multitude, and the LORD has blessed you wherever I turned. And now, when shall I also provide for my own house?"
verses.30:31: And he said, "What shall I give you?" And Jacob said, "You shall give me nothing at all. If you will do this thing for me, I will again tend and keep your flock:
verses.30:32: Let me pass through all your flock today, removing from there every speckled and spotted one, and every dark one among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats; and such shall be my wages.
verses.30:33: So my righteousness will answer for me in time to come, when you come concerning my wages in your presence: every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and dark among the sheep, shall be reckoned as stolen with me."
verses.30:34: And Laban said, "Behold, let it be according to your word!"
verses.30:35: So he removed on that day the male goats that were striped and spotted, and all the female goats that were speckled and spotted—every one that had white on it—and every dark one among the sheep, and put them into the hand of his sons.
verses.30:36: And he set a three days' journey between himself and Jacob, while Jacob pastured the remainder of Laban's flocks.
verses.30:37: Then Jacob took for himself fresh rods of poplar, almond, and plane tree, and peeled white strips in them, exposing the white that was in the rods.
verses.30:38: And he set the rods which he had peeled in the gutters, in the watering troughs where the flocks came to drink, directly in front of the flocks; and they mated when they came to drink.
verses.30:39: So the flocks mated before the rods, and the flocks brought forth young that were striped, speckled, and spotted.
verses.30:40: And Jacob separated the lambs, and set the faces of the flocks toward the striped and all the dark ones in the flock of Laban; and he set apart his own droves for himself, and did not put them with Laban's flock.
verses.30:41: And it came to pass, whenever the stronger of the flock were mating, that Jacob laid the rods before the eyes of the flock in the gutters, so that they might mate among the rods.
verses.30:42: But when the flock was feeble, he did not place them there; so the feebler became Laban's, and the stronger became Jacob's.
verses.30:43: Thus the man prospered exceedingly, and had abundant flocks, handmaids and menservants, and camels and donkeys.
verses.31:1: Now he heard the words of Laban's sons, saying, "Jacob has taken all that belonged to our father, and from what belonged to our father he has gained all this wealth."
verses.31:2: And Jacob saw the countenance of Laban, and behold, it was not toward him as in times past.
verses.31:3: Then the LORD said to Jacob, "Return to the land of your fathers and to your kindred, and I will be with you."
verses.31:4: So Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah to the field, to his flock.
verses.31:5: And he said to them, "I see your father's countenance, that it is not toward me as in times past; yet the God of my father has been with me.
verses.31:6: And you yourselves know that with all my strength I have served your father.
verses.31:7: Yet your father has deceived me and changed my wages ten times, but God did not permit him to harm me.
verses.31:8: If he spoke thus, 'The speckled shall be your wages,' then all the flock bore speckled; and if he spoke thus, 'The streaked shall be your wages,' then all the flock bore streaked.
verses.31:9: Thus God has taken away the livestock of your father and given it to me.
verses.31:10: And it came to pass at the time the flock conceived, that I lifted up my eyes and saw in a dream, and behold, the male goats leaping upon the flock were streaked, speckled, and dappled.
verses.31:11: Then the Angel of God said to me in the dream, 'Jacob.' And I said, 'Here I am.'
verses.31:12: And He said, 'Lift up your eyes now and see: all the male goats leaping upon the flock are streaked, speckled, and dappled; for I have seen all that Laban is doing to you.
verses.31:13: I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed a pillar and where you vowed a vow to Me. Now arise, go out from this land, and return to the land of your kindred.'"
verses.31:14: Then Rachel and Leah answered and said to him, "Is there still any portion or inheritance for us in our father's house?
verses.31:15: Are we not regarded as foreigners by him? For he has sold us, and has also completely consumed our money.
verses.31:16: For all the wealth that God has taken away from our father belongs to us and to our children. Now then, whatever God has said to you, do it."
verses.31:17: Then Jacob arose and set his sons and his wives upon the camels.
verses.31:18: And he drove away all his livestock and all his goods that he had gathered, the livestock of his possession that he had acquired in Paddan Aram, to go to his father Isaac in the land of Canaan.
verses.31:19: Now Laban had gone to shear his sheep, and Rachel stole the household idols that belonged to her father.
verses.31:20: And Jacob outwitted Laban the Aramean, by not telling him that he was fleeing.
verses.31:21: So he fled with all that he had, and arose and crossed the River, and set his face toward the hill country of Gilead.
verses.31:22: And it was told to Laban on the third day that Jacob had fled.
verses.31:23: Then he took his brethren with him and pursued after him a seven days' journey, and he overtook him in the hill country of Gilead.
verses.31:24: But God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream by night, and said to him, "Take heed to yourself, lest you speak to Jacob either good or bad."
verses.31:25: So Laban caught up with Jacob. Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the hill country, and Laban with his brethren pitched camp in the hill country of Gilead.
verses.31:26: And Laban said to Jacob, "What have you done, that you have outwitted me and led away my daughters like captives of the sword?
verses.31:27: Why did you flee in secret, and steal away from me, and did not tell me? For I would have sent you away with joy and with songs, with timbrel and harp.
verses.31:28: And you did not allow me to kiss my sons and my daughters. Now you have acted foolishly in so doing.
verses.31:29: It is in the power of my hand to do you harm, yet the God of your father spoke to me last night, saying, 'Take heed to yourself against speaking to Jacob either good or bad.'
verses.31:30: And now you have surely gone because you greatly longed for your father's house, yet why have you stolen my gods?"
verses.31:31: Then Jacob answered and said to Laban, "Because I was afraid, for I thought you might take your daughters away from me by force.
verses.31:32: With whomever you find your gods, he shall not live. In the presence of our brethren, identify for yourself what is with me and take it for yourself." For Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen them.
verses.31:33: So Laban went into Jacob's tent, and into Leah's tent, and into the tent of the two maidservants, but he did not find them. Then he went out of Leah's tent and entered Rachel's tent.
verses.31:34: Now Rachel had taken the household idols, put them in the camel's saddle, and sat upon them. And Laban searched through all the tent, but did not find them.
verses.31:35: And she said to her father, "May my lord not be angry that I cannot rise before you, for the manner of women is upon me." And he searched, but did not find the household idols.
verses.31:36: Then Jacob became angry and contended with Laban; and Jacob answered and said to Laban, "What is my transgression? What is my sin, that you have so hotly pursued me?
verses.31:37: Since you have searched through all my goods, what have you found of all your household articles? Set it here before my brethren and your brethren, that they may judge between the two of us.
verses.31:38: These twenty years I have been with you; your ewes and your female goats have not miscarried their young, and I have not eaten the rams of your flock.
verses.31:39: What was torn by wild beasts I did not bring to you; I myself bore the loss of it. From my hand you required it, whether stolen by day or stolen by night.
verses.31:40: There I was: by day the heat consumed me, and the frost by night, and my sleep departed from my eyes.
verses.31:41: Thus I have been twenty years in your house: I served you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years for your flock, and you have changed my wages ten times.
verses.31:42: Unless the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, had been with me, surely now you would have sent me away empty-handed. God has seen my affliction and the labor of my hands, and rebuked you last night."
verses.31:43: And Laban answered and said to Jacob, "These daughters are my daughters, and these children are my children, and this flock is my flock, and all that you see is mine. Yet what can I do this day to these daughters of mine, or to their children whom they have borne?
verses.31:44: Now therefore, come, let us make a covenant, you and I, and let it be a witness between me and you."
verses.31:45: So Jacob took a stone and set it up as a pillar.
verses.31:46: And Jacob said to his brethren, "Gather stones." And they took stones and made a heap, and they ate there upon the heap.
verses.31:47: And Laban called it Jegar Sahadutha, but Jacob called it Galeed.
verses.31:48: And Laban said, "This heap is a witness between me and you this day." Therefore its name was called Galeed. And Laban said to Jacob, "Behold this heap, and behold the pillar which I have set between me and you."
verses.31:49: And Mizpah, because he said, "May the LORD watch between me and you when we are absent one from another.
verses.31:50: If you afflict my daughters, or if you take wives besides my daughters, though no man is with us, see, God is witness between me and you.
verses.31:52: This heap is a witness, and the pillar is a witness, that I will not pass beyond this heap to you, and you will not pass beyond this heap and this pillar to me, for harm.
verses.31:53: May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor judge between us, the God of their father." And Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.
verses.31:54: Then Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain, and called his brethren to eat bread. And they ate bread and spent the night on the mountain.
verses.32:1: And Laban rose early in the morning, and kissed his sons and his daughters and blessed them. Then Laban departed and returned to his place.
verses.32:2: Now Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him.
verses.32:3: When Jacob saw them, he said, "This is the camp of God." Therefore he called the name of that place Mahanaim.
verses.32:4: Then Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother in the land of Seir, the country of Edom.
verses.32:5: And he commanded them, saying, "Thus you shall say to my lord Esau: 'Thus says your servant Jacob: I have sojourned with Laban and tarried until now.
verses.32:6: I have oxen and donkeys, flocks, and male and female servants; and I have sent to inform my lord, that I may find favor in your sight.'"
verses.32:7: Then the messengers returned to Jacob, saying, "We came to your brother Esau, and indeed he is coming to meet you, and four hundred men are with him."
verses.32:8: So Jacob was greatly afraid and distressed; and he divided the people who were with him, along with the flocks, the herds, and the camels, into two camps.
verses.32:9: And he said, "If Esau comes against the one camp and strikes it, then the remaining camp shall escape."
verses.32:10: Then Jacob said, "O God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, O LORD who said to me, 'Return to your land and to your kindred, and I will deal well with you,'
verses.32:11: I am unworthy of all the lovingkindnesses and all the faithfulness which You have shown to Your servant; for with only my staff I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.
verses.32:12: Deliver me, I pray, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau; for I fear him, lest he come and strike me—mother with children.
verses.32:13: Yet You said, 'I will surely do good to you, and make your descendants as the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude.'"
verses.32:14: So he lodged there that night, and took from what he had at hand a present for Esau his brother:
verses.32:15: two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams,
verses.32:16: thirty nursing camels with their colts, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten donkey colts.
verses.32:17: And he delivered them into the hand of his servants, each drove by itself, and said to his servants, "Cross over ahead of me, and put a space between drove and drove."
verses.32:18: And he commanded the first one, saying, "When Esau my brother meets you and asks you, saying, 'To whom do you belong, and where are you going, and whose are these ahead of you?'
verses.32:19: then you shall say, 'They belong to your servant Jacob; it is a present sent to my lord Esau, and behold, he also is behind us.'"
verses.32:20: And he likewise commanded the second, and the third, and all who followed the droves, saying, "After this manner you shall speak to Esau when you find him;
verses.32:21: and you shall say, 'Behold, your servant Jacob is also behind us.'" For he said, "I will appease him with the present that goes ahead of me, and afterward I will see his face; perhaps he will accept me."
verses.32:22: So the present crossed over before him, while he himself stayed that night in the camp.
verses.32:23: And he arose during that night and took his two wives, his two maidservants, and his eleven sons, and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.
verses.32:24: He took them and brought them across the stream, and sent across all that belonged to him.
verses.32:25: Then Jacob was left alone; and a Man wrestled with him until the breaking of the dawn.
verses.32:26: Now when He saw that He did not prevail against him, He touched the socket of his hip; and the socket of Jacob's hip was put out of joint as he wrestled with Him.
verses.32:27: And He said, "Let Me go, for the dawn is breaking." But he said, "I will not let You go unless You bless me."
verses.32:28: So He said to him, "What is your name?" And he answered, "Jacob."
verses.32:29: And He said, "No longer shall your name be called Jacob, but Israel; for you have contended with God and with men, and have prevailed."
verses.32:30: Then Jacob asked Him, saying, "Tell me, I pray, Your name." And He said, "Why is it that you ask for My name?" And He blessed him there.
verses.32:31: So Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: "For I have seen God face to face, and yet my life has been delivered."
verses.32:32: And the sun rose upon him as he passed beyond Penuel, and he was limping because of his hip.
verses.32:33: Therefore the children of Israel do not eat the sinew of the thigh which is upon the socket of the hip, to this day, because He touched the socket of Jacob's hip at the sinew of the thigh.
verses.33:1: Now Jacob lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, Esau was coming, and with him four hundred men. So he divided the children among Leah, Rachel, and the two maidservants.
verses.33:2: And he placed the maidservants and their children in front, Leah and her children after them, and Rachel and Joseph last.
verses.33:3: Then he himself went on before them and bowed to the ground seven times, until he drew near to his brother.
verses.33:4: But Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell upon his neck and kissed him; and they wept.
verses.33:5: And he lifted up his eyes and saw the women and the children, and said, "Who are these with you?" And he said, "The children whom God has graciously given your servant."
verses.33:6: Then the maidservants drew near, they and their children, and bowed down.
verses.33:7: Leah also drew near with her children, and they bowed down. Afterward Joseph and Rachel drew near, and they bowed down.
verses.33:8: Then he said, "What do you mean by all this company which I encountered?" And he answered, "To find favor in the sight of my lord."
verses.33:9: But Esau said, "I have plenty, my brother; keep what is yours for yourself."
verses.33:10: And Jacob said, "No, I pray, if indeed I have found favor in your sight, then accept my present from my hand; for I have seen your face as though seeing the face of God, and you have received me favorably.
verses.33:11: Take, I pray, my blessing that has been brought to you, because God has dealt graciously with me, and because I have everything." So he urged him, and he accepted it.
verses.33:12: Then he said, "Let us set out and go on our way, and I will go before you."
verses.33:13: But he said to him, "My lord knows that the children are tender, and the nursing flocks and herds are a care to me; if they are driven hard for one day, all the flocks will die.
verses.33:14: Let my lord, I pray, pass on ahead of his servant, and I will move along gently at the pace of the livestock before me and at the pace of the children, until I come to my lord in Seir."
verses.33:15: And Esau said, "Let me leave with you some of the people who are with me." But he said, "What need is there? Only let me find favor in the sight of my lord."
verses.33:16: So Esau returned that day on his way to Seir.
verses.33:17: And Jacob journeyed to Succoth, and built himself a house and made booths for his livestock. Therefore he called the name of the place Succoth.
verses.33:18: Then Jacob arrived safely at the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Paddan Aram; and he pitched his camp before the city.
verses.33:19: And he purchased the parcel of the field where he had pitched his tent from the hand of the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, for one hundred pieces of money.
verses.33:20: Then he erected an altar there and called it El Elohe Israel.
verses.34:1: Now Dinah, the daughter of Leah, whom she had borne to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.
verses.34:2: And Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the land, saw her; and he took her and lay with her and violated her.
verses.34:3: And his soul clung to Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the young woman and spoke tenderly to the young woman.
verses.34:4: Then Shechem spoke to Hamor his father, saying, "Get me this young girl as a wife."
verses.34:5: Now Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter; and his sons were with his livestock in the field, so Jacob held his peace until they came.
verses.34:6: And Hamor the father of Shechem went out to Jacob to speak with him.
verses.34:7: And the sons of Jacob came in from the field when they heard it; and the men were grieved and exceedingly angry, because he had committed a disgraceful deed in Israel by lying with the daughter of Jacob, for such a thing ought not to be done.
verses.34:8: And Hamor spoke with them, saying, "The soul of my son Shechem longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as a wife.
verses.34:9: And intermarry with us: give your daughters to us, and take our daughters for yourselves.
verses.34:10: So you shall dwell with us, and the land shall be before you. Dwell and trade in it, and acquire possessions in it."
verses.34:11: Then Shechem said to her father and to her brothers, "Let me find favor in your sight, and whatever you say to me I will give.
verses.34:12: Set upon me ever so great a bride-price and gift, and I will give just as you say to me; only give me the young woman as a wife."
verses.34:13: But the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father with deceit and spoke thus, because he had defiled Dinah their sister.
verses.34:14: And they said to them, "We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to a man who is uncircumcised, for that is a reproach to us.
verses.34:15: Only on this condition will we consent to you: if you will become like us, in that every male among you is circumcised.
verses.34:16: Then we will give our daughters to you, and we will take your daughters for ourselves; and we will dwell with you, and we will become one people.
verses.34:17: But if you will not listen to us to be circumcised, then we will take our daughter and depart."
verses.34:18: And their words were pleasing in the eyes of Hamor and in the eyes of Shechem, the son of Hamor.
verses.34:19: So the young man did not delay to do the thing, because he delighted in the daughter of Jacob; and he was more honored than all the house of his father.
verses.34:20: And Hamor and Shechem his son came to the gate of their city and spoke to the men of their city, saying,
verses.34:21: "These men are at peace with us; therefore let them dwell in the land and trade in it, for behold, the land is spacious before them. Let us take their daughters to ourselves as wives, and let us give them our daughters.
verses.34:22: Only on this condition will the men consent to dwell with us, to become one people: if every male among us is circumcised just as they are circumcised.
verses.34:23: Will not their livestock, their property, and all their beasts be ours? Only let us consent to them, and they will dwell with us."
verses.34:24: And all who went out of the gate of his city listened to Hamor and to Shechem his son; and every male was circumcised, all who went out of the gate of his city.
verses.34:25: Now it came to pass on the third day, when they were in pain, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, the brothers of Dinah, each took his sword and came upon the city unawares, and slew every male.
verses.34:26: And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah from the house of Shechem and went out.
verses.34:27: The sons of Jacob came upon the slain and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister.
verses.34:28: They took their flocks and their herds and their donkeys, and what was in the city and what was in the field.
verses.34:29: And all their wealth, all their little ones, and their wives they took captive; and they plundered all that was in the houses.
verses.34:30: Then Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, "You have brought trouble upon me by making me odious among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites; and since I am few in number, they will gather themselves together against me and strike me, and I shall be destroyed, both I and my household."
verses.34:31: And they said, "Should he treat our sister as a harlot?"
verses.35:1: Then God said to Jacob, "Arise, go up to Bethel and dwell there; and make an altar there to God, who appeared to you when you fled from the face of Esau your brother."
verses.35:2: And Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him, "Put away the foreign gods that are among you, purify yourselves, and change your garments.
verses.35:3: And let us arise and go up to Bethel; and I will make an altar there to God, who answered me in the day of my distress and has been with me in the way which I have gone."
verses.35:4: So they gave to Jacob all the foreign gods that were in their hands, and the earrings that were in their ears; and Jacob hid them under the terebinth tree that was by Shechem.
verses.35:5: And they journeyed, and the terror of God was upon the cities that were all around them, and they did not pursue the sons of Jacob.
verses.35:6: So Jacob came to Luz, which is in the land of Canaan—that is, Bethel—he and all the people who were with him.
verses.35:7: And he built an altar there and called the place El-Bethel, because there God revealed Himself to him when he fled from the face of his brother.
verses.35:8: Now Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died, and she was buried below Bethel under the oak; and he called its name Allon-Bacuth.
verses.35:9: Then God appeared to Jacob again, when he came from Paddan-Aram, and blessed him.
verses.35:10: And God said to him, "Your name is Jacob; your name shall not be called Jacob any longer, but Israel shall be your name." So He called his name Israel.
verses.35:11: Also God said to him, "I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall proceed from you, and kings shall come forth from your loins.
verses.35:12: And the land which I gave to Abraham and to Isaac I will give to you, and to your seed after you I will give the land."
verses.35:13: Then God went up from him in the place where He had spoken with him.
verses.35:14: And Jacob set up a pillar in the place where He had spoken with him, a pillar of stone; and he poured out a drink offering upon it, and poured oil upon it.
verses.35:15: And Jacob called the name of the place where God had spoken with him, Bethel.
verses.35:16: Then they journeyed from Bethel; and while there was still some distance to come to Ephrath, Rachel went into labor, and she had hard labor. And Israel journeyed and pitched his tent beyond the tower of Eder.
verses.35:17: Now it came to pass, when she was in hard labor, that the midwife said to her, "Do not fear, for this also is a son for you."
verses.35:18: And so it was, as her soul was departing—for she died—that she called his name Ben-Oni; but his father called him Benjamin.
verses.35:19: So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath—that is, Bethlehem.
verses.35:20: And Jacob set a pillar upon her grave; that is the pillar of Rachel's grave to this day.
verses.35:22: And it came to pass, while Israel dwelt in that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father's concubine; and Israel heard of it. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve:
verses.35:23: The sons of Leah were Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, and Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun;
verses.35:24: the sons of Rachel were Joseph and Benjamin;
verses.35:25: the sons of Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant, were Dan and Naphtali;
verses.35:26: and the sons of Zilpah, Leah's maidservant, were Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob who were born to him in Paddan-Aram.
verses.35:27: Then Jacob came to his father Isaac at Mamre, Kiriath-Arba—that is, Hebron—where Abraham and Isaac had sojourned.
verses.35:28: Now the days of Isaac were one hundred and eighty years.
verses.35:29: So Isaac breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people, old and full of days; and his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.
verses.36:1: Now these are the generations of Esau, that is, Edom.
verses.36:2: Esau took his wives from among the daughters of Canaan: Adah the daughter of Elon the Hittite, Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite,
verses.36:3: and Basemath the daughter of Ishmael, the sister of Nebaioth.
verses.36:4: And Adah bore Eliphaz to Esau, and Basemath bore Reuel.
verses.36:5: And Oholibamah bore Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These were the sons of Esau who were born to him in the land of Canaan.
verses.36:6: Then Esau took his wives, his sons, his daughters, and all the souls of his household, together with his livestock, all his beasts, and all his possessions that he had acquired in the land of Canaan, and departed to a land away from his brother Jacob.
verses.36:7: For their substance was too great for them to dwell together, and the land of their sojourning could not sustain them on account of their livestock.
verses.36:8: So Esau dwelt in Mount Seir—Esau is Edom.
verses.36:9: And these are the generations of Esau, the father of Edom, in Mount Seir.
verses.36:10: These are the names of the sons of Esau: Eliphaz the son of Adah the wife of Esau, and Reuel the son of Basemath the wife of Esau.
verses.36:11: And the sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz.
verses.36:12: Now Timna was concubine to Eliphaz the son of Esau, and she bore Amalek to Eliphaz. These were the sons of Adah the wife of Esau.
verses.36:13: And these were the sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These were the sons of Basemath the wife of Esau.
verses.36:14: And these were the sons of Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon, the wife of Esau; she bore to Esau Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
verses.36:15: These were the chiefs of the sons of Esau. The sons of Eliphaz, the firstborn of Esau: Chief Teman, Chief Omar, Chief Zepho, Chief Kenaz,
verses.36:16: Chief Korah, Chief Gatam, and Chief Amalek. These were the chiefs of Eliphaz in the land of Edom; these were the sons of Adah.
verses.36:17: And these were the sons of Reuel the son of Esau: Chief Nahath, Chief Zerah, Chief Shammah, and Chief Mizzah. These were the chiefs of Reuel in the land of Edom; these were the sons of Basemath the wife of Esau.
verses.36:18: And these were the sons of Oholibamah the wife of Esau: Chief Jeush, Chief Jalam, and Chief Korah. These were the chiefs of Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, the wife of Esau.
verses.36:19: These were the sons of Esau, and these were their chiefs—that is, Edom.
verses.36:20: These were the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
verses.36:21: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These were the chiefs of the Horites, the sons of Seir, in the land of Edom.
verses.36:22: And the sons of Lotan were Hori and Hemam; and Lotan's sister was Timna.
verses.36:23: And these were the sons of Shobal: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
verses.36:24: And these were the sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah. This was the Anah who found the hot springs in the wilderness as he tended the donkeys of his father Zibeon.
verses.36:25: And these were the children of Anah: Dishon, and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah.
verses.36:26: And these were the sons of Dishan: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
verses.36:27: These were the sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
verses.36:28: These were the sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
verses.36:29: These were the chiefs of the Horites: Chief Lotan, Chief Shobal, Chief Zibeon, Chief Anah,
verses.36:30: Chief Dishon, Chief Ezer, and Chief Dishan. These were the chiefs of the Horites, according to their chiefs, in the land of Seir.
verses.36:31: Now these were the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the children of Israel.
verses.36:32: Bela the son of Beor reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
verses.36:33: When Bela died, Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his place.
verses.36:34: When Jobab died, Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.
verses.36:35: When Husham died, Hadad the son of Bedad, who struck down Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his place; and the name of his city was Avith.
verses.36:36: When Hadad died, Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his place.
verses.36:37: When Samlah died, Shaul of Rehoboth by the River reigned in his place.
verses.36:38: When Shaul died, Baal-Hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his place.
verses.36:39: When Baal-Hanan the son of Achbor died, Hadar reigned in his place; the name of his city was Pau, and the name of his wife was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.
verses.36:40: Now these are the names of the chiefs of Esau, according to their clans, according to their places, by their names: Chief Timna, Chief Alvah, Chief Jetheth,
verses.36:41: Chief Oholibamah, Chief Elah, Chief Pinon,
verses.36:42: Chief Kenaz, Chief Teman, Chief Mibzar,
verses.36:43: Chief Magdiel, and Chief Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom, according to their dwelling places in the land of their possession. He is Esau, the father of Edom.
verses.37:1: Now Jacob dwelt in the land where his father had sojourned, in the land of Canaan.
verses.37:2: These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph, being seventeen years old, was tending the flock with his brethren; and he was a youth with the sons of Bilhah and with the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives. And Joseph brought an evil report concerning them to their father.
verses.37:3: Now Israel loved Joseph above all his sons, for he was the son of his old age; and he made for him a tunic of many colors.
verses.37:4: And his brethren saw that their father loved him above all his brethren; so they hated him, and they could not speak to him in peace.
verses.37:5: Now Joseph dreamed a dream and declared it to his brethren, and they hated him yet more.
verses.37:6: And he said to them, "Please hear this dream which I have dreamed:
verses.37:7: Behold, we were binding sheaves in the midst of the field, and behold, my sheaf arose and also stood upright; and behold, your sheaves came around and bowed down to my sheaf."
verses.37:8: Then his brethren said to him, "Will you truly reign over us? Or will you truly rule over us?" So they hated him yet more for his dreams and for his words.
verses.37:9: Then he dreamed yet another dream and recounted it to his brethren, and said, "Behold, I have dreamed a dream once more; and behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me."
verses.37:10: And he recounted it to his father and to his brethren; and his father rebuked him and said to him, "What is this dream which you have dreamed? Shall we indeed come, I and your mother and your brethren, to bow down to you to the ground?"
verses.37:11: And his brethren envied him, but his father kept the matter in mind.
verses.37:12: Now his brethren went to pasture their father's flock in Shechem.
verses.37:13: And Israel said to Joseph, "Are not your brethren pasturing the flock in Shechem? Come, and I will send you to them." And he said to him, "Here I am."
verses.37:14: Then he said to him, "Go now, see to the welfare of your brethren and the welfare of the flock, and bring back word to me." So he sent him out from the Valley of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.
verses.37:15: And a certain man found him, and behold, he was wandering in the field. And the man asked him, saying, "What do you seek?"
verses.37:16: So he said, "I am seeking my brethren. Tell me, please, where they are pasturing the flock."
verses.37:17: And the man said, "They have departed from here, for I heard them saying, 'Let us go to Dothan.'" So Joseph went after his brethren and found them in Dothan.
verses.37:18: Now they saw him from afar, and before he drew near to them, they conspired against him to put him to death.
verses.37:19: And they said one to another, "Behold, this master of dreams is coming!
verses.37:20: Now therefore, come and let us slay him and cast him into one of the pits; and we shall say, 'An evil beast has devoured him.' Then we shall see what will become of his dreams."
verses.37:21: But Reuben heard it and delivered him out of their hand, and said, "Let us not take his life."
verses.37:22: And Reuben said to them, "Shed no blood, but cast him into this pit which is in the wilderness, and do not lay a hand upon him"—that he might deliver him out of their hand, to restore him to his father.
verses.37:23: So it came to pass, when Joseph came to his brethren, that they stripped Joseph of his tunic, the tunic of many colors that was upon him.
verses.37:24: And they took him and cast him into the pit. Now the pit was empty; there was no water in it.
verses.37:25: Then they sat down to eat bread. And they lifted up their eyes and looked, and behold, a caravan of Ishmaelites was coming from Gilead, with their camels bearing spices, balm, and myrrh, going to carry them down to Egypt.
verses.37:26: And Judah said to his brethren, "What profit is there if we slay our brother and conceal his blood?
verses.37:27: Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites, and do not let our hand be upon him, for he is our brother, our own flesh." And his brethren heeded him.
verses.37:28: Then Midianite traders passed by; so they drew and lifted Joseph up out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver. And they brought Joseph to Egypt.
verses.37:29: Then Reuben returned to the pit, and behold, Joseph was not in the pit; and he tore his garments.
verses.37:30: And he returned to his brethren and said, "The lad is no more! And as for me, where shall I go?"
verses.37:31: So they took Joseph's tunic, slaughtered a male goat, and dipped the tunic in the blood.
verses.37:32: Then they sent the tunic of many colors and brought it to their father, and said, "We have found this. Please identify whether it is your son's tunic or not."
verses.37:33: And he recognized it and said, "It is my son's tunic! An evil beast has devoured him. Surely Joseph has been torn in pieces!"
verses.37:34: Then Jacob tore his clothes, put sackcloth upon his loins, and mourned for his son many days.
verses.37:35: And all his sons and all his daughters arose to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted; and he said, "For I shall go down into Sheol to my son, mourning." Thus his father wept for him.
verses.37:36: Meanwhile the Medanites sold him into Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard.
verses.38:1: Now it came to pass at that time that Judah went down from his brethren and turned aside to a certain Adullamite man, whose name was Hirah.
verses.38:2: And Judah saw there a daughter of a certain Canaanite man, whose name was Shua; and he took her and went in to her.
verses.38:3: So she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Er.
verses.38:4: And she conceived again and bore a son, and she called his name Onan.
verses.38:5: And she yet again bore a son, and she called his name Shelah. Now he was at Chezib when she bore him.
verses.38:6: Then Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.
verses.38:7: But Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the LORD; and the LORD put him to death.
verses.38:8: And Judah said to Onan, "Go in to your brother's wife and perform the duty of a brother-in-law to her, and raise up offspring for your brother."
verses.38:9: But Onan knew that the offspring would not be his; and it came to pass, whenever he went in to his brother's wife, that he wasted it on the ground, so as not to give offspring to his brother.
verses.38:10: And what he did was evil in the sight of the LORD; therefore He put him to death also.
verses.38:11: Then Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, "Remain a widow in your father's house until Shelah my son grows up." For he said, "Lest he also die like his brethren." So Tamar went and dwelt in her father's house.
verses.38:12: Now in the course of many days, the daughter of Shua, Judah's wife, died. And when Judah was comforted, he went up to the shearers of his flock at Timnah, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.
verses.38:13: And it was told to Tamar, saying, "Behold, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his flock."
verses.38:14: So she put off her widow's garments from herself, covered herself with a veil, and wrapped herself, and sat at the entrance of Enaim, which is by the way to Timnah; for she saw that Shelah had grown up, and she had not been given to him as a wife.
verses.38:15: When Judah saw her, he supposed her to be a harlot, because she had covered her face.
verses.38:16: Then he turned aside to her by the way and said, "Come now, let me come in to you"—for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, "What will you give me, that you may come in to me?"
verses.38:17: And he said, "I will send a young goat from the flock." And she said, "Only if you give a pledge until you send it."
