verses.38:18: Then he said, "What pledge shall I give you?" So she said, "Your signet and your cord, and your staff that is in your hand." And he gave them to her and went in to her, and she conceived by him.
verses.38:19: Then she arose and departed, and laid aside her veil from herself, and put on her widow's garments.
verses.38:20: And Judah sent the young goat by the hand of his friend the Adullamite, to receive the pledge from the woman's hand; but he did not find her.
verses.38:21: Then he asked the men of her place, saying, "Where is the temple harlot who was at Enaim by the wayside?" And they said, "There has been no temple harlot in this place."
verses.38:22: So he returned to Judah and said, "I did not find her; and also the men of the place said, 'There has been no temple harlot in this place.'"
verses.38:23: And Judah said, "Let her keep them for herself, lest we become an object of scorn; behold, I sent this young goat, and you did not find her."
verses.38:24: And it came to pass, about three months later, that it was told to Judah, saying, "Tamar your daughter-in-law has played the harlot; and moreover, behold, she is with child by harlotry." So Judah said, "Bring her out and let her be burned!"
verses.38:25: As she was being brought out, she sent word to her father-in-law, saying, "By the man to whom these belong, I am with child." And she said, "Please identify to whom these belong—the signet, the cords, and the staff."
verses.38:26: Then Judah recognized them and said, "She is more righteous than I, because I did not give her to Shelah my son." And he did not know her again.
verses.38:27: Now it came to pass, at the time of her giving birth, that behold, twins were in her womb.
verses.38:28: And it came to pass, as she was giving birth, that one put out a hand; and the midwife took a scarlet thread and bound it upon his hand, saying, "This one came out first."
verses.38:29: Then it came to pass, as he drew back his hand, that behold, his brother came out; and she said, "What a breach you have made for yourself!" Therefore his name was called Perez.
verses.38:30: And afterward his brother came out, upon whose hand was the scarlet thread; and his name was called Zerah.
verses.39:1: Now Joseph had been brought down to Egypt, and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard, an Egyptian, purchased him from the hand of the Ishmaelites who had brought him down there.
verses.39:2: And the LORD was with Joseph, and he became a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
verses.39:3: And his master saw that the LORD was with him, and that the LORD caused all that he did to prosper in his hand.
verses.39:4: So Joseph found favor in his sight and attended him; and he appointed him over his house, and all that he possessed he placed in his hand.
verses.39:5: And it came to pass, from the time that he appointed him in his house and over all that he possessed, that the LORD blessed the house of the Egyptian on account of Joseph; and the blessing of the LORD was upon all that he had, both in the house and in the field.
verses.39:6: Thus he left all that he had in the hand of Joseph, and with him he did not concern himself with anything except the bread which he ate. Now Joseph was handsome in form and fair in appearance.
verses.39:7: And it came to pass after these things that his master's wife lifted up her eyes toward Joseph, and she said, "Lie with me."
verses.39:8: But he refused and said to his master's wife, "Behold, with me here my master does not know what is in the house, and he has committed all that he possesses into my hand.
verses.39:9: He is no greater in this house than I, nor has he withheld anything from me except you, because you are his wife. How then can I commit this great wickedness, and sin against God?"
verses.39:10: And it came to pass, as she spoke to Joseph day by day, that he did not heed her, to lie beside her or to be with her.
verses.39:11: And it happened on a certain day that he came into the house to perform his work, and not one of the men of the house was there inside the house.
verses.39:12: And she caught hold of him by his garment, saying, "Lie with me!" But he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and went outside.
verses.39:13: And it came to pass, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand and had fled outside,
verses.39:14: that she called to the men of her house and spoke to them, saying, "See, he has brought in to us a Hebrew man to mock us! He came in to me to lie with me, and I cried out with a loud voice.
verses.39:15: And it came to pass, when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried out, that he left his garment beside me, and fled, and went outside."
verses.39:16: And she laid his garment beside her until his master came to his house.
verses.39:17: And she spoke to him with words like these, saying, "The Hebrew servant whom you brought to us came in to me to mock me;
verses.39:18: and it came to pass, as I lifted up my voice and cried out, that he left his garment beside me and fled outside."
verses.39:19: And it came to pass, when his master heard the words of his wife which she spoke to him, saying, "In this manner your servant dealt with me," that his wrath was kindled.
verses.39:20: Then Joseph's master took him and put him into the prison, the place where the king's prisoners were confined; and he was there in the prison.
verses.39:21: But the LORD was with Joseph and extended lovingkindness to him, and He granted him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
verses.39:22: And the keeper of the prison committed into Joseph's hand all the prisoners who were in the prison; and whatever was done there, he was the one who did it.
verses.39:23: The keeper of the prison did not inspect anything that was in his hand, because the LORD was with him; and whatever he did, the LORD caused to prosper.
verses.40:1: And it came to pass after these things that the cupbearer of the king of Egypt and the baker offended their lord, the king of Egypt.
verses.40:2: And Pharaoh was angry with his two officers, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.
verses.40:3: So he put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place where Joseph was confined.
verses.40:4: And the captain of the guard appointed Joseph to be with them, and he attended to them; and they remained in custody for some time.
verses.40:5: Then both of them dreamed a dream, each man his own dream in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream—the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were confined in the prison.
verses.40:6: And Joseph came in to them in the morning and looked upon them, and behold, they were dejected.
verses.40:7: So he asked Pharaoh's officers who were with him in the custody of his master's house, saying, "Why are your countenances downcast today?"
verses.40:8: And they said to him, "We have dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter for it." Then Joseph said to them, "Do not interpretations belong to God? Please tell them to me."
verses.40:9: So the chief cupbearer recounted his dream to Joseph, and said to him, "In my dream, behold, a vine was before me;
verses.40:10: and on the vine were three branches. It was as though it budded; its blossom shot forth, and its clusters ripened into grapes.
verses.40:11: And Pharaoh's cup was in my hand; so I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh's cup, and placed the cup upon Pharaoh's palm."
verses.40:12: And Joseph said to him, "This is its interpretation: the three branches are three days.
verses.40:13: Within three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore you to your office; and you shall place Pharaoh's cup into his hand according to the former custom, when you were his cupbearer.
verses.40:14: Only remember me with yourself when it goes well with you, and please show kindness to me; make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.
verses.40:15: For truly I was stolen away from the land of the Hebrews; and here also I have done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon."
verses.40:16: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was favorable, he said to Joseph, "I also was in my dream, and behold, three baskets of white bread were upon my head.
verses.40:17: And in the uppermost basket were all manner of foods for Pharaoh, the work of a baker; and the birds were eating them out of the basket upon my head."
verses.40:18: Then Joseph answered and said, "This is its interpretation: the three baskets are three days.
verses.40:19: Within three days Pharaoh will lift up your head from off you and hang you on a tree; and the birds shall eat your flesh from off you."
verses.40:20: And it came to pass on the third day, which was Pharaoh's birthday, that he made a feast for all his servants; and he lifted up the head of the chief cupbearer and the head of the chief baker in the midst of his servants.
verses.40:21: And he restored the chief cupbearer to his office as cupbearer, and he placed the cup upon Pharaoh's palm.
verses.40:22: But the chief baker he hanged, just as Joseph had interpreted to them.
verses.40:23: Yet the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph, but forgot him.
verses.41:1: And it came to pass, at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh was dreaming, and behold, he stood by the Nile.
verses.41:2: And behold, seven cows came up out of the Nile, fair in appearance and plump in flesh, and they grazed in the reed grass.
verses.41:3: And behold, seven other cows came up after them out of the Nile, ugly in appearance and gaunt in flesh, and stood beside the cows on the bank of the Nile.
verses.41:4: And the cows that were ugly in appearance and gaunt in flesh devoured the seven cows that were fair in appearance and plump. Then Pharaoh awoke.
verses.41:5: And he slept and dreamed a second time; and behold, seven heads of grain were growing on one stalk, plump and good.
verses.41:6: And behold, seven heads of grain, thin and scorched by the east wind, sprouted up after them.
verses.41:7: And the thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven plump and full heads. Then Pharaoh awoke, and behold, it was a dream.
verses.41:8: And it came to pass in the morning that his spirit was troubled, so he sent and summoned all the magicians of Egypt and all its wise men. And Pharaoh recounted his dream to them, but there was no one who could interpret them to Pharaoh.
verses.41:9: Then the chief cupbearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, "I call to mind my offenses this day.
verses.41:10: Pharaoh was angry with his servants, and he placed me in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, both me and the chief baker.
verses.41:11: And we dreamed a dream on one night, I and he; each of us dreamed according to the interpretation of his own dream.
verses.41:12: Now a young Hebrew man was there with us, a servant of the captain of the guard. And we told him, and he interpreted our dreams for us; to each man he interpreted according to his dream.
verses.41:13: And it came to pass, just as he interpreted to us, so it happened: me he restored to my office, and him he hanged."
verses.41:14: Then Pharaoh sent and summoned Joseph, and they brought him swiftly out of the dungeon; and he shaved, changed his garments, and came to Pharaoh.
verses.41:15: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it. Yet I have heard it said of you that when you hear a dream, you can interpret it."
verses.41:16: And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, "It is not in me; God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace."
verses.41:17: Then Pharaoh spoke to Joseph: "In my dream, behold, I was standing on the bank of the Nile.
verses.41:18: And behold, seven cows came up out of the Nile, plump in flesh and fair in form, and they grazed in the reed grass.
verses.41:19: And behold, seven other cows came up after them, poor, exceedingly ugly in form, and lean in flesh; I have never seen the like of them in all the land of Egypt for ugliness.
verses.41:20: And the lean and ugly cows devoured the first seven plump cows.
verses.41:21: Yet when they had gone into their inward parts, no one could tell that they had gone into them, for their appearance was just as ugly as at the beginning. Then I awoke.
verses.41:22: And I saw in my dream, and behold, seven heads of grain were growing on one stalk, full and good.
verses.41:23: And behold, seven heads of grain, withered, thin, and scorched by the east wind, sprouted up after them.
verses.41:24: And the thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven good heads. So I told this to the magicians, but there was no one who could declare it to me."
verses.41:25: Then Joseph said to Pharaoh, "The dream of Pharaoh is one; God has declared to Pharaoh what He is about to do.
verses.41:26: The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven good heads of grain are seven years; the dream is one.
verses.41:27: And the seven lean and ugly cows that came up after them are seven years, and the seven empty heads of grain scorched by the east wind shall be seven years of famine.
verses.41:28: This is the word which I have spoken to Pharaoh: what God is about to do, He has shown to Pharaoh.
verses.41:29: Behold, seven years of great abundance are coming throughout all the land of Egypt,
verses.41:30: and after them seven years of famine shall arise, and all the abundance shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land.
verses.41:31: So the abundance shall not be known in the land because of that famine which follows, for it shall be exceedingly severe.
verses.41:32: And as for the repeating of the dream to Pharaoh twice, it is because the matter is firmly established by God, and God will swiftly bring it to pass.
verses.41:33: Now therefore, let Pharaoh seek out a discerning and wise man, and set him over the land of Egypt.
verses.41:34: Let Pharaoh act and appoint overseers over the land, and collect a fifth part of the land of Egypt during the seven years of abundance.
verses.41:35: And let them gather all the food of these good years that are coming, and store up grain under the hand of Pharaoh for food in the cities, and guard it.
verses.41:36: Then that food shall be a reserve for the land for the seven years of famine which shall be in the land of Egypt, that the land may not be cut off by the famine."
verses.41:37: And the counsel was good in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of all his servants.
verses.41:38: And Pharaoh said to his servants, "Can we find a man like this, in whom is the Spirit of God?"
verses.41:39: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Since God has made all this known to you, there is no one as discerning and wise as you.
verses.41:40: You shall be over my house, and by your command all my people shall be governed; only in the throne shall I be greater than you."
verses.41:41: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "See, I have set you over all the land of Egypt."
verses.41:42: Then Pharaoh removed his signet ring from his hand and put it on Joseph's hand; and he clothed him in garments of fine linen and placed a chain of gold around his neck.
verses.41:43: And he had him ride in his second chariot, and they cried out before him, "Bow the knee!" Thus he set him over all the land of Egypt.
verses.41:44: Pharaoh also said to Joseph, "I am Pharaoh, and without you no man shall lift his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt."
verses.41:45: And Pharaoh called Joseph's name Zaphenath-Paneah. And he gave him Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On, as a wife. So Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.
verses.41:46: Now Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh and passed through all the land of Egypt.
verses.41:47: During the seven years of abundance, the earth brought forth by handfuls.
verses.41:48: So he gathered up all the food of the seven years which were in the land of Egypt and laid up the food in the cities; the food from the fields surrounding each city he stored within it.
verses.41:49: And Joseph heaped up grain in great abundance, like the sand of the sea, until he ceased counting it, for it was without number.
verses.41:50: And to Joseph were born two sons before the year of famine arrived, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On, bore to him.
verses.41:51: Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh: "For God has made me forget all my toil and all my father's house."
verses.41:52: And the name of the second he called Ephraim: "For God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction."
verses.41:53: Then the seven years of abundance which had been in the land of Egypt came to an end,
verses.41:54: and the seven years of famine began to come, just as Joseph had said. There was famine in all the lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.
verses.41:55: Then all the land of Egypt was famished, and the people cried out to Pharaoh for bread. And Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, "Go to Joseph; whatever he says to you, do."
verses.41:56: And the famine was over all the face of the earth, and Joseph opened all the storehouses and sold grain to the Egyptians. And the famine grew severe in the land of Egypt.
verses.41:57: And all the earth came to Egypt to Joseph to buy grain, because the famine was severe in all the earth.
verses.42:1: And Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt, and Jacob said to his sons, "Why do you gaze at one another?"
verses.42:2: And he said, "Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy grain for us from that place, that we may live and not die."
verses.42:3: So ten of Joseph's brethren went down to buy grain from Egypt.
verses.42:4: But Jacob did not send Benjamin, Joseph's brother, with his brethren, for he said, "Lest calamity befall him."
verses.42:5: And the sons of Israel came to buy grain among those who were coming, for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
verses.42:6: Now Joseph was the ruler over the land; it was he who sold grain to all the people of the land. And Joseph's brethren came and bowed down before him with their faces to the earth.
verses.42:7: And Joseph saw his brethren and recognized them, yet he acted as a stranger toward them and spoke harsh words with them. And he said to them, "From where have you come?" And they said, "From the land of Canaan, to buy food."
verses.42:8: Thus Joseph recognized his brethren, but they did not recognize him.
verses.42:9: And Joseph remembered the dreams which he had dreamed concerning them, and he said to them, "You are spies! You have come to see the nakedness of the land."
verses.42:10: And they said to him, "No, my lord; rather, your servants have come to buy food.
verses.42:11: All of us are sons of one man. We are honest men; your servants have not been spies."
verses.42:12: And he said to them, "No, but you have come to see the nakedness of the land."
verses.42:13: And they said, "Your servants are twelve brethren, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and behold, the youngest is this day with our father, and one is no more."
verses.42:14: And Joseph said to them, "It is just as I spoke to you, saying, 'You are spies!'
verses.42:15: By this you shall be tested: by the life of Pharaoh, you shall not go out from this place unless your youngest brother comes here.
verses.42:16: Send one of you, and let him bring your brother, while you shall be kept in custody, that your words may be tested to see whether truth is with you; and if not, by the life of Pharaoh, surely you are spies."
verses.42:17: So he put them all together into custody for three days.
verses.42:18: And Joseph said to them on the third day, "Do this and live, for I fear God:
verses.42:19: If you are honest men, let one of your brethren be bound in your prison house, and you go, carry grain for the famine of your households.
verses.42:20: And bring your youngest brother to me, so that your words may be verified, and you shall not die." And they did so.
verses.42:21: Then they said one to another, "Truly we are guilty concerning our brother, because we saw the distress of his soul when he pleaded with us, and we did not listen; therefore this distress has come upon us."
verses.42:22: And Reuben answered them, saying, "Did I not speak to you, saying, 'Do not sin against the boy,' and you did not listen? Therefore behold, his blood also is now required."
verses.42:23: Now they did not know that Joseph understood them, for there was an interpreter between them.
verses.42:24: And he turned away from them and wept. Then he returned to them and spoke with them, and he took Simeon from them and bound him before their eyes.
verses.42:25: Then Joseph gave a command to fill their vessels with grain, and to restore every man's silver to his sack, and to give them provisions for the journey. And thus it was done for them.
verses.42:26: So they loaded their grain upon their donkeys and departed from there.
verses.42:27: And as one of them opened his sack to give fodder to his donkey at the lodging place, he saw his silver; and behold, it was in the mouth of his bag.
verses.42:28: And he said to his brethren, "My silver has been returned, and behold, it is right here in my bag!" Then their hearts failed them, and they turned trembling one to another, saying, "What is this that God has done to us?"
verses.42:29: Then they came to Jacob their father in the land of Canaan and told him all that had befallen them, saying,
verses.42:30: "The man, the lord of the land, spoke harshly with us and treated us as spies of the land.
verses.42:31: And we said to him, 'We are honest men; we have not been spies.
verses.42:32: We are twelve brethren, sons of our father; one is no more, and the youngest is this day with our father in the land of Canaan.'
verses.42:33: Then the man, the lord of the land, said to us, 'By this I shall know that you are honest men: leave one of your brethren with me, and take grain for the famine of your households, and go.
verses.42:34: And bring your youngest brother to me, so that I may know that you are not spies, but that you are honest men. Then I will deliver your brother to you, and you may trade in the land.'"
verses.42:35: And it came to pass, as they were emptying their sacks, that behold, every man's bundle of silver was in his sack; and when they and their father saw the bundles of their silver, they were afraid.
verses.42:36: And Jacob their father said to them, "You have bereaved me! Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more, and you would take Benjamin; all these things are against me."
verses.42:37: Then Reuben spoke to his father, saying, "You may slay my two sons if I do not bring him back to you; entrust him into my hand, and I will restore him to you."
verses.42:38: But he said, "My son shall not go down with you, for his brother is dead, and he alone remains. If calamity should befall him on the way in which you go, then you would bring down my gray hair in sorrow to Sheol."
verses.43:1: Now the famine was severe in the land.
verses.43:2: And it came to pass, when they had finished eating the grain which they had brought from Egypt, that their father said to them, "Return, buy for us a little food."
verses.43:3: Then Judah spoke to him, saying, "The man solemnly warned us, saying, 'You shall not see my face unless your brother is with you.'
verses.43:4: If you will send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you.
verses.43:5: But if you will not send him, we will not go down; for the man said to us, 'You shall not see my face unless your brother is with you.'"
verses.43:6: And Israel said, "Why have you dealt so ill with me as to tell the man whether you still had a brother?"
verses.43:7: And they said, "The man inquired closely concerning us and our kindred, saying, 'Is your father still alive? Have you another brother?' And we answered him according to the tenor of these words. Could we in any way know that he would say, 'Bring your brother down'?"
verses.43:8: Then Judah said to Israel his father, "Send the lad with me, and let us arise and go, that we may live and not die—both we and you, and also our little ones.
verses.43:9: I myself will be surety for him; from my hand you shall require him. If I do not bring him back to you and set him before you, then let me bear the blame before you forever.
verses.43:10: For if we had not delayed, surely by now we would have returned this second time."
verses.43:11: And Israel their father said to them, "If it must be so, then do this: take some of the choice produce of the land in your vessels and carry down a present for the man—a little balm and a little honey, spices and myrrh, pistachio nuts and almonds.
verses.43:12: And take double the silver in your hand, and the silver that was returned in the mouth of your bags carry back in your hand; perhaps it was an oversight.
verses.43:13: Take your brother also, and arise, return to the man.
verses.43:14: And may God Almighty grant you mercy before the man, that he may release to you your other brother and Benjamin. As for me, if I am bereaved, I am bereaved."
verses.43:15: So the men took that present, and they took double the silver in their hand, along with Benjamin; and they arose and went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
verses.43:16: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the steward of his house, "Bring the men into the house, and slaughter an animal and make preparations, for the men shall eat with me at noon."
verses.43:17: And the man did just as Joseph had spoken, and the man brought the men into Joseph's house.
verses.43:18: Now the men were afraid because they were brought into Joseph's house, and they said, "It is on account of the silver that was returned in our bags the first time that we are being brought in, so that he may seek an occasion against us and fall upon us, to take us as slaves, together with our donkeys."
verses.43:19: So they drew near to the steward of Joseph's house and spoke to him at the doorway of the house,
verses.43:20: and said, "O my lord, we indeed came down the first time to buy food;
verses.43:21: and it came to pass, when we arrived at the lodging place and opened our bags, that behold, every man's silver was in the mouth of his bag, our silver in its full weight; so we have brought it back in our hand.
verses.43:22: And we have brought down other silver in our hand to buy food. We do not know who placed our silver in our bags."
verses.43:23: But he said, "Peace be to you, do not be afraid. Your God and the God of your father has given you treasure in your bags; your silver came to me." Then he brought Simeon out to them.
verses.43:24: So the man brought the men into Joseph's house and gave them water, and they washed their feet; and he gave fodder to their donkeys.
verses.43:25: And they made ready the present for Joseph's coming at noon, for they had heard that they were to eat bread there.
verses.43:26: When Joseph came into the house, they brought to him the present that was in their hand into the house, and bowed down before him to the earth.
verses.43:27: Then he asked them about their well-being and said, "Is your father well, the old man of whom you spoke? Is he still alive?"
verses.43:28: And they said, "Your servant our father is well; he is still alive." And they bowed their heads and prostrated themselves.
verses.43:29: Then he lifted up his eyes and saw his brother Benjamin, his mother's son, and said, "Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me?" And he said, "May God be gracious to you, my son."
verses.43:30: And Joseph hurried out, for his heart yearned deeply for his brother, and he sought a place to weep; so he entered his inner chamber and wept there.
verses.43:31: Then he washed his face and came out, and he restrained himself and said, "Serve the meal."
verses.43:32: So they served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves; because the Egyptians could not eat bread with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination to the Egyptians.
verses.43:33: And they were seated before him, the firstborn according to his birthright and the youngest according to his youth; and the men looked in astonishment one at another.
verses.43:34: And he sent portions to them from before him, yet Benjamin's portion was five times as great as the portion of any of them. So they drank and made merry with him.
verses.44:1: And he commanded the one who was over his house, saying, "Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they are able to carry, and place each man's money in the mouth of his sack.
verses.44:2: And my cup, the silver cup, you shall place in the mouth of the youngest one's sack, together with the money for his grain." And he did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.
verses.44:3: When the morning grew light, the men were sent on their way, they and their donkeys.
verses.44:4: They had gone out of the city and were not yet far off, when Joseph said to the one who was over his house, "Arise, pursue the men; and when you overtake them, say to them, 'Why have you repaid evil for good?
verses.44:5: Is this not the one from which my lord drinks, and with which he indeed practices divination? You have done evil in what you have done.'"
verses.44:6: So he overtook them and spoke these words to them.
verses.44:7: And they said to him, "Why does my lord speak such words as these? Far be it from your servants to do anything like this!
verses.44:8: Behold, the money that we found in the mouths of our sacks we returned to you from the land of Canaan; how then could we steal silver or gold from your lord's house?
verses.44:9: With whomever among your servants it is found, let him die; and we also will be bondservants to my lord."
verses.44:10: And he said, "Even now let it be according to your words: the one with whom it is found shall be my bondservant, and you shall be blameless."
verses.44:11: Then they hurried, and each man lowered his sack to the ground, and each man opened his sack.
verses.44:12: And he searched, beginning with the oldest and ending with the youngest; and the cup was found in Benjamin's sack.
verses.44:13: Then they tore their garments, and each man loaded his donkey, and they returned to the city.
verses.44:14: And Judah and his brothers came to Joseph's house, for he was still there; and they fell before him to the ground.
verses.44:15: And Joseph said to them, "What is this deed that you have done? Did you not know that a man such as I can indeed practice divination?"
verses.44:16: And Judah said, "What shall we say to my lord? What shall we speak, and how shall we justify ourselves? God has found out the iniquity of your servants. Behold, we are my lord's bondservants, both we and he in whose hand the cup was found."
verses.44:17: But he said, "Far be it from me to do this! The man in whose hand the cup was found, he shall be my bondservant; but as for you, go up in peace to your father."
verses.44:18: Then Judah drew near to him and said, "Oh, my lord, please let your servant speak a word in the ears of my lord, and do not let your wrath burn against your servant; for you are even as Pharaoh.
verses.44:19: My lord questioned his servants, saying, 'Do you have a father or a brother?'
verses.44:20: And we said to my lord, 'We have an aged father, and a young child of his old age; his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother, and his father loves him.'
verses.44:21: Then you said to your servants, 'Bring him down to me, that I may set my eyes upon him.'
verses.44:22: And we said to my lord, 'The lad cannot leave his father; for if he should leave his father, his father would die.'
verses.44:23: But you said to your servants, 'Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you shall not see my face again.'
verses.44:24: And it came to pass, when we went up to your servant my father, that we told him the words of my lord.
verses.44:25: And our father said, 'Go back and buy us a little food.'
verses.44:26: But we said, 'We cannot go down. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down; for we cannot see the man's face if our youngest brother is not with us.'
verses.44:27: Then your servant my father said to us, 'You know that my wife bore me two sons;
verses.44:28: and the one went out from me, and I said, "Surely he has been torn in pieces!" and I have not seen him until now.
verses.44:29: And if you take this one also from before my face, and harm befalls him, then you shall bring down my gray hair in affliction to Sheol.'
verses.44:30: Now therefore, when I come to your servant my father, and the lad is not with us—seeing that his soul is bound up in the lad's soul—
verses.44:31: it shall come to pass, when he sees that the lad is not with us, that he will die. Thus your servants shall bring down the gray hair of your servant our father with grief to Sheol.
verses.44:32: For your servant became surety for the lad to my father, saying, 'If I do not bring him back to you, then I shall bear the guilt before my father all my days.'
verses.44:33: Now therefore, please let your servant remain in place of the lad as a bondservant to my lord, and let the lad go up with his brothers.
verses.44:34: For how shall I go up to my father if the lad is not with me, lest I look upon the calamity that would come upon my father?"
verses.45:1: Then Joseph could no longer restrain himself before all those who stood attending him, and he cried out, "Send every man out from before me!" So no one stood with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
verses.45:2: And he lifted up his voice in weeping, so that the Egyptians heard it, and the household of Pharaoh heard it.
verses.45:3: And Joseph said to his brothers, "I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?" But his brothers could not answer him, for they were dismayed before his presence.
verses.45:4: Then Joseph said to his brothers, "Please draw near to me." So they drew near. And he said, "I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
verses.45:5: Now therefore, do not be grieved nor angry with yourselves because you sold me here; for God sent me ahead of you to preserve life.
verses.45:6: For these two years the famine has been in the midst of the land, and there remain five years in which there shall be neither plowing nor harvest.
verses.45:7: And God sent me before you to preserve for you a remnant in the earth, and to keep you alive through a great deliverance.
verses.45:8: So now, it was not you who sent me here, but God; and He has appointed me a father to Pharaoh, and lord over all his house, and ruler throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.45:9: Hasten and go up to my father, and say to him, 'Thus says your son Joseph: God has made me lord of all Egypt; come down to me, do not delay.
verses.45:10: And you shall dwell in the land of Goshen, and you shall be near to me, you and your sons and your sons' sons, your flocks and your herds, and all that you possess.
verses.45:11: And there I will sustain you, for there are yet five years of famine, lest you and your household and all that you have come to poverty.'
verses.45:12: And behold, your own eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my own mouth speaking to you.
verses.45:13: So you shall declare to my father all my glory in Egypt, and all that you have seen; and you shall hasten and bring my father down here."
verses.45:14: Then he fell upon his brother Benjamin's neck and wept, and Benjamin wept upon his neck.
verses.45:15: Moreover he kissed all his brothers and wept over them; and after that his brothers spoke with him.
verses.45:16: Now the report was heard in Pharaoh's house, saying, "Joseph's brothers have come." And it was pleasing in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of his servants.
verses.45:17: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Say to your brothers, 'Do this: load your beasts and depart, go to the land of Canaan,
verses.45:18: and take your father and your households and come to me; and I will give you the best of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat the fat of the land.'
verses.45:19: Now you are commanded, 'Do this: take for yourselves wagons from the land of Egypt for your little ones and for your wives, and bring your father and come.
verses.45:20: And do not let your eyes look with regret upon your goods, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.'"
verses.45:21: And the sons of Israel did so; and Joseph gave them wagons, according to the command of Pharaoh, and he gave them provisions for the journey.
verses.45:22: To all of them he gave, to each man, changes of garments; but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of garments.
verses.45:23: And to his father he sent as follows: ten donkeys laden with the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys laden with grain, bread, and sustenance for his father for the journey.
verses.45:24: So he sent his brothers away, and they departed; and he said to them, "Do not quarrel along the way."
verses.45:25: Then they went up out of Egypt, and came to the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father.
verses.45:26: And they told him, saying, "Joseph is still alive, and indeed he is ruler over all the land of Egypt." And his heart grew numb, for he did not believe them.
verses.45:27: Yet when they spoke to him all the words of Joseph which he had spoken to them, and when he saw the wagons that Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob their father revived.
verses.45:28: And Israel said, "It is enough! Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die."
verses.46:1: Then Israel set forth with all that belonged to him, and came to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.
verses.46:2: And God spoke to Israel in visions of the night and said, "Jacob, Jacob!" And he said, "Here I am."
verses.46:3: Then He said, "I am God, the God of your father; do not fear to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there.
verses.46:4: I Myself will go down with you to Egypt, and I will also surely bring you up again; and Joseph shall place his hand upon your eyes."
verses.46:5: Then Jacob arose from Beersheba; and the sons of Israel carried Jacob their father, their little ones, and their wives in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent to carry him.
verses.46:6: And they took their livestock and their goods which they had acquired in the land of Canaan, and came to Egypt—Jacob and all his offspring with him.
verses.46:7: His sons and his sons' sons with him, his daughters and his sons' daughters, and all his offspring he brought with him into Egypt.
verses.46:8: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel who came into Egypt, Jacob and his sons: the firstborn of Jacob was Reuben.
verses.46:9: And the sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
verses.46:10: And the sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman.
verses.46:11: And the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
verses.46:12: And the sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah—but Er and Onan had died in the land of Canaan. And the sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.
verses.46:13: And the sons of Issachar: Tola, Puvah, Job, and Shimron.
verses.46:14: And the sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
verses.46:15: These were the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Paddan Aram, along with his daughter Dinah; all the souls of his sons and his daughters were thirty-three.
verses.46:16: And the sons of Gad: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
verses.46:17: And the sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and Serah their sister; and the sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
verses.46:18: These were the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah his daughter; and these she bore to Jacob, sixteen souls.
verses.46:19: The sons of Rachel, Jacob's wife: Joseph and Benjamin.
verses.46:20: And to Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On, bore to him.
verses.46:21: And the sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.
verses.46:22: These were the sons of Rachel who were born to Jacob: fourteen souls in all.
verses.46:23: And the sons of Dan: Hushim.
verses.46:24: And the sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
verses.46:25: These were the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter, and she bore these to Jacob: seven souls in all.
verses.46:26: All the souls belonging to Jacob who came to Egypt, who came forth from his loins, besides the wives of Jacob's sons, were sixty-six souls in all.
verses.46:27: And the sons of Joseph who were born to him in Egypt were two souls; all the souls of the house of Jacob who came into Egypt were seventy.
verses.46:28: Now he sent Judah ahead of him to Joseph, to point out the way before him to Goshen; and they came into the land of Goshen.
verses.46:29: So Joseph made ready his chariot and went up to Goshen to meet Israel his father; and he presented himself to him, and fell upon his neck, and wept upon his neck a long while.
verses.46:30: And Israel said to Joseph, "Now let me die, since I have seen your face, because you are still alive."
verses.46:31: Then Joseph said to his brethren and to his father's household, "I will go up and report to Pharaoh, and say to him, 'My brethren and my father's household, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me.
verses.46:32: And the men are shepherds, for they have been keepers of livestock; and they have brought their flocks, their herds, and all that belongs to them.'
verses.46:33: And it shall come to pass, when Pharaoh calls for you and says, 'What is your occupation?'
verses.46:34: that you shall say, 'Your servants have been keepers of livestock from our youth even until now, both we and also our fathers,' that you may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians."
verses.47:1: Then Joseph went in and reported to Pharaoh, and said, "My father and my brethren, with their flocks and their herds and all that belongs to them, have come from the land of Canaan; and behold, they are in the land of Goshen."
verses.47:2: And he took five men from among his brethren and presented them before Pharaoh.
verses.47:3: Then Pharaoh said to his brethren, "What is your occupation?" And they said to Pharaoh, "Your servants are shepherds, both we and also our fathers."
verses.47:4: And they said to Pharaoh, "We have come to sojourn in the land, for there is no pasture for the flocks of your servants, because the famine is severe in the land of Canaan. Now therefore, please let your servants dwell in the land of Goshen."
verses.47:5: Then Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying, "Your father and your brethren have come to you.
verses.47:6: The land of Egypt is before you; have your father and your brethren dwell in the best of the land—let them dwell in the land of Goshen. And if you know that there are capable men among them, then appoint them as overseers of livestock over what belongs to me."
verses.47:7: Then Joseph brought in Jacob his father and set him before Pharaoh; and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
verses.47:8: And Pharaoh said to Jacob, "How many are the days of the years of your life?"
verses.47:9: And Jacob said to Pharaoh, "The days of the years of my sojourning are one hundred and thirty years; few and evil have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not attained to the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their sojourning."
verses.47:10: So Jacob blessed Pharaoh and went out from before Pharaoh.
verses.47:11: And Joseph settled his father and his brethren, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
verses.47:12: Then Joseph sustained his father, his brethren, and all his father's household with bread, according to the number of their little ones.
verses.47:13: Now there was no bread in all the land, for the famine was exceedingly severe, so that the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan languished because of the famine.
verses.47:14: And Joseph gathered up all the money that was found in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan, for the grain which they were buying; and Joseph brought the money into Pharaoh's house.
verses.47:15: So when the money was exhausted in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came to Joseph, saying, "Give us bread! Why should we die in your presence? For the money is gone."
verses.47:16: Then Joseph said, "Give your livestock, and I will give you food in exchange for your livestock, if the money is gone."
verses.47:17: So they brought their livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for the horses, the flocks, the herds, and the donkeys. Thus he sustained them with bread in exchange for all their livestock that year.
verses.47:18: When that year had ended, they came to him in the second year and said to him, "We will not conceal from my lord that our money is spent, and the herds of livestock belong to my lord; nothing remains before my lord except our bodies and our land.
verses.47:19: Why should we perish before your eyes, both we and our land? Buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants to Pharaoh; and give us seed, that we may live and not die, and that the land may not become desolate."
verses.47:20: Then Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, for every Egyptian sold his field, because the famine prevailed over them; so the land became Pharaoh's.
verses.47:21: And as for the people, he removed them into the cities, from one end of the borders of Egypt even to the other end.
verses.47:22: Only the land of the priests he did not buy; for the priests had an allotment from Pharaoh, and they ate their allotment which Pharaoh gave them; therefore they did not sell their land.
verses.47:23: Then Joseph said to the people, "Behold, I have bought you and your land this day for Pharaoh. Look, here is seed for you, and you shall sow the land.
verses.47:24: And it shall come to pass at the harvests that you shall give one-fifth to Pharaoh; and four-fifths shall be your own, as seed for the field and for your food, for those of your households, and as food for your little ones."
verses.47:25: So they said, "You have saved our lives; let us find favor in the sight of my lord, and we will be Pharaoh's servants."
verses.47:26: And Joseph made it a statute over the land of Egypt to this day, that Pharaoh should have one-fifth; only the land of the priests alone did not become Pharaoh's.
verses.47:27: So Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen; and they gained possessions in it, and were fruitful and multiplied exceedingly.
verses.47:28: And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years; so the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were one hundred and forty-seven years.
verses.47:29: When the days of Israel drew near for him to die, he called his son Joseph and said to him, "If now I have found favor in your sight, please put your hand under my thigh, and deal with me in lovingkindness and truth: please do not bury me in Egypt,
verses.47:30: but let me lie with my fathers; you shall carry me out of Egypt and bury me in their burial place." And he said, "I will do as you have spoken."
verses.47:31: Then he said, "Swear to me." And he swore to him. So Israel bowed himself upon the head of the bed.
verses.48:1: Now it came to pass after these things that Joseph was told, "Behold, your father is sick." So he took his two sons with him, Manasseh and Ephraim.
verses.48:2: And someone told Jacob and said, "Behold, your son Joseph is coming to you." Then Israel strengthened himself and sat up on the bed.
verses.48:3: And Jacob said to Joseph, "God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan and blessed me,
verses.48:4: and He said to me, 'Behold, I will make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will make of you an assembly of peoples, and I will give this land to your seed after you as an everlasting possession.'
verses.48:5: And now your two sons, who were born to you in the land of Egypt before I came to you in Egypt, are mine; Ephraim and Manasseh shall be mine, just as Reuben and Simeon are.
verses.48:6: But your offspring whom you father after them shall be yours; they shall be called by the name of their brethren in their inheritance.
verses.48:7: And as for me, when I came from Paddan, Rachel died beside me in the land of Canaan on the way, when there was still a short distance to go to Ephrath; and I buried her there on the way to Ephrath—that is, Bethlehem."
verses.48:8: Then Israel saw the sons of Joseph and said, "Who are these?"
verses.48:9: And Joseph said to his father, "They are my sons, whom God has given me in this place." And he said, "Please bring them to me, that I may bless them."
verses.48:10: Now the eyes of Israel were dim because of old age, so that he could not see. Then Joseph brought them near to him, and he kissed them and embraced them.
verses.48:11: And Israel said to Joseph, "I did not expect to see your face, and behold, God has let me see your seed also."
verses.48:12: Then Joseph brought them out from beside his knees, and he bowed down with his face to the earth.
verses.48:13: And Joseph took them both, Ephraim with his right hand toward Israel's left hand, and Manasseh with his left hand toward Israel's right hand, and brought them near to him.
verses.48:14: But Israel stretched out his right hand and laid it upon the head of Ephraim, though he was the younger, and his left hand upon the head of Manasseh, crossing his hands, for Manasseh was the firstborn.
verses.48:15: And he blessed Joseph and said, "The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has shepherded me all my life to this day,
verses.48:16: the Angel who has redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads; and let my name be called upon them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; and let them multiply abundantly in the midst of the earth."
verses.48:17: When Joseph saw that his father had laid his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, it was displeasing in his sight; so he took hold of his father's hand to move it from the head of Ephraim to the head of Manasseh.
verses.48:18: And Joseph said to his father, "Not so, my father, for this one is the firstborn; place your right hand upon his head."
verses.48:19: But his father refused and said, "I know, my son, I know. He also shall become a people, and he also shall be great; yet indeed his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a fullness of nations."
verses.48:20: And he blessed them that day, saying, "By you Israel shall pronounce blessing, saying, 'May God make you as Ephraim and as Manasseh.'" Thus he set Ephraim before Manasseh.
verses.48:21: Then Israel said to Joseph, "Behold, I am dying, yet God will be with you and bring you back to the land of your fathers.
verses.48:22: Moreover, I have given to you one portion above your brethren, which I took from the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow."
verses.49:1: And Jacob called his sons and said, "Gather yourselves together, that I may declare to you what shall befall you in the latter days:
verses.49:2: Assemble and hear, you sons of Jacob, and listen to Israel your father.
verses.49:3: Reuben, you are my firstborn, my might and the firstfruits of my vigor, preeminent in dignity and preeminent in power.
verses.49:4: Turbulent as water, you shall not have preeminence, because you went up to your father's bed; then you defiled it—he went up to my couch!
verses.49:5: Simeon and Levi are brothers; weapons of violence are their swords.
verses.49:6: May my soul not enter their council, and may my glory not be joined to their assembly; for in their anger they slew a man, and in their self-will they hamstrung an ox.
verses.49:7: Cursed be their anger, for it is fierce, and their wrath, for it is cruel! I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel.
verses.49:8: Judah, you are the one whom your brethren shall praise; your hand shall be upon the neck of your enemies; your father's sons shall bow down before you.
verses.49:9: Judah is a lion's cub; from the prey, my son, you have gone up. He crouches, he lies down like a lion, and like a lioness—who shall rouse him?
verses.49:10: The scepter shall not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes; and to him shall be the obedience of the peoples.
verses.49:11: Tying his foal to the vine, and his donkey's colt to the choice vine, he washes his garments in wine, and his robe in the blood of grapes.
verses.49:12: His eyes are darker than wine, and his teeth are whiter than milk.
verses.49:13: Zebulun shall dwell at the shore of the seas; he shall become a haven for ships, and his border shall be toward Sidon.
verses.49:14: Issachar is a sturdy donkey, lying down between the sheepfolds.
verses.49:15: He saw that rest was good and that the land was pleasant; so he bowed his shoulder to bear burdens and became subject to forced labor.
verses.49:16: Dan shall judge his people as one of the tribes of Israel.
verses.49:17: Dan shall be a serpent by the way, a viper by the path, that bites the heels of the horse so that its rider falls backward.
verses.49:18: I have waited for Your salvation, O LORD!
verses.49:19: Gad—raiders shall raid him, yet he shall raid at their heel.
verses.49:20: From Asher his bread shall be rich, and he shall yield royal delicacies.
verses.49:21: Naphtali is a doe let loose; he utters words of beauty.
verses.49:22: Joseph is a fruitful bough, a fruitful bough beside a spring; his branches climb over the wall.
verses.49:23: The archers bitterly assailed him; they shot at him and harried him;
verses.49:24: yet his bow remained steadfast, and the arms of his hands were made agile by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob—from there is the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel—
verses.49:25: by the God of your father, who will help you, and by the Almighty, who will bless you with blessings of heaven above, blessings of the deep that lies beneath, blessings of the breasts and of the womb.
verses.49:26: The blessings of your father have surpassed the blessings of my forefathers, up to the utmost bound of the everlasting hills; may they be upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the head of the one set apart among his brethren.
verses.49:27: Benjamin is a ravenous wolf: in the morning he devours the prey, and at evening he divides the spoil."
verses.49:28: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is what their father spoke to them as he blessed them; he blessed each one according to his own blessing.
verses.49:29: Then he charged them and said to them, "I am about to be gathered to my people; bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,
verses.49:30: in the cave that is in the field of Machpelah, which is before Mamre in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought along with the field from Ephron the Hittite as a burial possession.
verses.49:31: There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife, there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife, and there I buried Leah.
verses.49:32: The purchase of the field and of the cave that is in it was from the sons of Heth."
verses.49:33: And when Jacob had finished commanding his sons, he drew his feet up into the bed, breathed his last, and was gathered to his people.
verses.50:1: And Joseph fell upon the face of his father, and wept over him, and kissed him.
verses.50:2: Then Joseph commanded his servants, the physicians, to embalm his father; and the physicians embalmed Israel.
verses.50:3: Forty days were fulfilled for him, for thus the days of embalming are fulfilled; and the Egyptians wept for him seventy days.
verses.50:4: When the days of weeping for him had passed, Joseph spoke to the household of Pharaoh, saying, "If now I have found favor in your sight, speak, I pray, in the ears of Pharaoh, saying,
verses.50:5: 'My father made me swear, saying, "Behold, I am dying; in my grave which I have dug for myself in the land of Canaan, there you shall bury me." Now therefore, let me go up, I pray, and bury my father, and I will return.'"
verses.50:6: And Pharaoh said, "Go up and bury your father, just as he made you swear."
verses.50:7: So Joseph went up to bury his father; and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,
verses.50:8: as well as all the house of Joseph, his brethren, and his father's house; only their little ones, their flocks, and their herds they left in the land of Goshen.
verses.50:9: Both chariots and horsemen also went up with him, and the company was exceedingly great.
verses.50:10: And they came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, and there they lamented with a great and exceedingly grievous lamentation; and he observed seven days of mourning for his father.
verses.50:11: When the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, they said, "This is a grievous mourning for the Egyptians." Therefore its name was called Abel Mizraim, which is beyond the Jordan.
verses.50:12: So his sons did for him just as he had commanded them.
verses.50:13: For his sons carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, the field which Abraham bought for a burial possession from Ephron the Hittite, facing Mamre.
verses.50:14: Then Joseph returned to Egypt—he and his brethren and all who had gone up with him to bury his father—after he had buried his father.
verses.50:15: When Joseph's brethren saw that their father was dead, they said, "Perhaps Joseph will bear a grudge against us and will surely repay us for all the evil which we did to him."
verses.50:16: So they sent word to Joseph, saying, "Your father commanded before his death, saying,
verses.50:17: 'Thus you shall say to Joseph: "I beg you, please forgive the transgression of your brethren and their sin, for they did evil to you."' And now, please forgive the transgression of the servants of the God of your father." And Joseph wept when they spoke to him.
verses.50:18: Then his brethren also went and fell down before him, and they said, "Behold, we are your servants."
verses.50:19: And Joseph said to them, "Do not fear, for am I in the place of God?
verses.50:20: As for you, you purposed evil against me, yet God purposed it for good, to accomplish what is done this day, to preserve many people alive.
verses.50:21: Now therefore, do not fear; I will sustain you and your little ones." Thus he comforted them and spoke to their hearts.
verses.50:22: So Joseph dwelt in Egypt, he and his father's house; and Joseph lived one hundred and ten years.
verses.50:23: And Joseph saw Ephraim's children to the third generation; the sons of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were also born upon Joseph's knees.
verses.50:24: And Joseph said to his brethren, "I am dying; yet God will surely visit you and bring you up from this land to the land of which He swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob."
verses.50:25: Then Joseph made the sons of Israel swear, saying, "God will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from here."
verses.50:26: So Joseph died, being one hundred and ten years old; and they embalmed him, and he was placed in a coffin in Egypt.

notes.1:1: Masoretic Hebrew reads plural hashshamayim ('the heavens') with the verb bara ('created').
notes.1:2: Hebrew tohu wavohu ('unformed and empty') is a rhyming pair describing uninhabitable emptiness; ruach Elohim ('Spirit of God,' or 'mighty wind from God') is paired with merachephet ('hovered,' cf. Deut 32:11).
notes.1:5: Hebrew yom echad uses the cardinal numeral ('one day'), whereas days two through five use anarthrous ordinals ('a second day,' etc.) and day six adds the definite article ('the sixth day,' v. 31).
notes.1:6: Hebrew raqia ('firmament') denotes a beaten-out vault or expanse dividing the waters.
notes.1:26: Hebrew adam ('man' or 'mankind') is paired with the plural verb 'let them have dominion,' marking humanity collectively as male and female (v. 27).
notes.2:2: Masoretic Hebrew reads 'the seventh day' (differing from the Septuagint's 'sixth day'); the completed verb wayekhal is rendered pluperfect ('had completed') to convey that God's work stood finished as the seventh day began.
notes.2:3: Literally 'which God created to make' (bara Elohim la'asot), a Hebrew idiom summarizing all that God had creatively fashioned.
notes.2:7: Hebrew plays on ha'adam ('the man') and ha'adamah ('the ground'); nephesh chayyah ('living soul') denotes a living, breathing being.
notes.2:14: Hebrew Hiddekel is rendered by its standard English name Tigris; qidmat Ashshur means 'east of Assyria.'
notes.2:18: Hebrew ezer kenegdo literally means 'a helper as opposite/corresponding to him,' denoting an equal, fitting counterpart.
notes.2:23: Hebrew wordplay pairs ishshah ('woman') with ish ('man').
notes.3:1: Hebrew arum ('crafty') plays on arumim ('naked') in 2:25. Throughout vv. 1-5 the serpent and the woman use second-person plural verbs and suffixes.
notes.3:8: Hebrew leruach hayyom literally means 'at the breeze/wind of the day,' denoting the cool afternoon breeze.
notes.3:15: Masoretic Hebrew uses masculine hu ('he,' agreeing with masculine zera, 'seed') and repeats the same rare verb shuph ('strike' or 'bruise') in both clauses.
notes.3:19: Hebrew appekha is literally 'your nostrils' or 'your face.'
notes.3:20: Hebrew Chawwah ('Eve') is linked by sound with chay ('living').
notes.4:1: Hebrew Qayin (Cain) plays on the verb qaniti ("I have acquired"). The Hebrew preposition literally reads "with the LORD," conveying "with the help of the LORD."
notes.4:7: Hebrew se'et literally means "a lifting up," likely referring to the lifting up of one's countenance or acceptance before God.
notes.4:8: The Masoretic Text records no spoken words after "spoke to Abel his brother." Ancient versions including the Septuagint, Samaritan Pentateuch, and Vulgate supply "Let us go out into the field."
notes.4:13: Hebrew avon can signify either "iniquity" or the "punishment" for iniquity, and the closing phrase can mean either "too great to bear" or "too great to be forgiven."
notes.4:25: Hebrew Shet (Seth) echoes the verb shat ("has appointed"), tying the son's name directly to Eve's words.
notes.5:2: Hebrew adam serves both as the personal name Adam and as the collective noun for humanity ("Man").
notes.5:24: Breaking the genealogy's refrain "and he died," the Hebrew states literally of Enoch "and he was not, for God took him," signifying his departure without experiencing death.
notes.5:29: Hebrew Noach (Noah) echoes the sound of yenachamenu ("shall comfort us") and recalls the Hebrew root meaning "rest."
notes.6:3: The rare Hebrew verb yadon occurs only here in Scripture and is understood either as "abide" (following ancient versions) or "contend/strive" (from the judicial root meaning to judge or plead).
notes.6:4: "Nephilim" transliterates the Masoretic Hebrew term, which is traditionally associated with the root meaning "to fall" and was rendered "giants" in the Septuagint and Vulgate.
notes.6:14: "Gopher wood" renders an unidentified Hebrew timber name occurring only here; the verse also features a deliberate wordplay between the verb "coat" (kaphar) and the noun "pitch" (kopher).
notes.6:16: The Hebrew noun tsohar appears in this architectural sense only here and denotes a window, skylight, or elevated light-opening beneath the roofline.
notes.7:2: The doubled numeral "seven seven" may denote either seven pairs or seven individuals of each clean kind, and "a male and his mate" renders the vivid Hebrew idiom literally meaning "a man and his wife."
notes.7:11: "Floodgates of the heavens" translates Hebrew arubbot hashamayim, literally "windows" or "lattices of the heavens," picturing the heavenly sluices releasing waters from above.
notes.7:23: The Masoretic vocalization of the opening verb is active (Qal, "and He blotted out"), taking God as the implicit subject before the direct object marker, followed by the passive Niphal ("and they were blotted out").
notes.8:13: Hebrew distinguishes the verb here (charvu, indicating that standing surface water had drained away) from the verb in verse 14 (yavshah, indicating that the ground itself had dried thoroughly).
notes.8:17: Ketiv/Qere: the written text reads hotse and the read text (Qere) reads haytse; both are Hiphil imperatives meaning "bring forth," with the Qere preserving an older orthographic form retaining the root yod.
notes.8:21: "The soothing aroma" (reach hannichoach) echoes the sound of Noah's name (Noach), recalling the hope of rest and relief expressed at his birth in Genesis 5:29.
notes.9:13: The Hebrew noun qeshet literally means 'bow' (both a warrior's bow and a rainbow), set here in the cloud as a sign of peace between God and the earth.
notes.9:21: The Masoretic text preserves the archaic orthographic form oholoh ('his tent') written with a final heh rather than the usual vav suffix.
notes.9:26: The poetic pronominal suffix lamo ('to him' or 'to them') appears here and in verse 27, signifying Canaan's servitude.
notes.9:27: The blessing plays on the name Japheth with the Hebrew verb yaft ('may He enlarge'). While 'he' traditionally refers to Japheth dwelling in Shem's tents, some interpreters take God as the subject.
notes.10:6: Mizraim is the standard Hebrew name for Egypt, preserved here in its ancestral genealogical form.
notes.10:11: The Hebrew clause may be read with Nimrod as the subject going forth into Assyria, or alternatively with Asshur as the subject ('From that land Asshur went forth').
notes.10:21: The Hebrew phrasing 'brother of Japheth the elder' is grammatically open and may also be rendered 'the elder brother of Japheth.'
notes.10:25: The name Peleg echoes the Hebrew verb niflegah ('was divided'), associating his lifetime with the division of the earth's peoples.
notes.11:2: Hebrew miqqedem can mean either 'from the east' or 'eastward'; here it introduces the migration into the Mesopotamian plain of Shinar.
notes.11:9: The name Babel (Babylon) is linked by wordplay to the Hebrew verb balal, meaning 'to confuse' or 'to confound.'
notes.11:28: Literally 'upon the face of Terah his father,' a Hebrew idiom meaning 'in the presence of' or 'during the lifetime of' his father.
notes.11:31: The Masoretic Hebrew reads 'they set out with them,' indicating that Terah and Abram departed together with Lot and Sarai as one company.
notes.12:3: Hebrew uses two distinct verbs here: qalal ('treat lightly' or 'disdain,' singular) for an opponent of Abram, and arar ('pronounce a solemn curse') for the LORD's judgment. The verb translated 'shall be blessed' may also carry a reflexive nuance, 'shall bless themselves.'
notes.12:9: The Negev is the arid southern region of Canaan, lying south of the hill country of Judah.
notes.12:14: The Hebrew text employs the archaic Pentateuchal spelling of the feminine pronoun 'she' (read hi), which also appears in verses 18 and 19.
notes.13:2: The Hebrew adjective kaved literally means 'heavy,' an idiom denoting abundant wealth in livestock and precious metals.
notes.13:8: Literally 'men, brothers,' a Hebrew idiom for close kinsmen—here uncle and nephew.
notes.13:10: Hebrew kikkar ('circle' or 'basin') denotes the broad, fertile alluvial plain of the lower Jordan valley.
notes.14:1: Hebrew "Goiim" literally means "nations" and here designates a region or coalition of peoples.
notes.14:15: Hebrew literally reads "to the left of Damascus," denoting north from an eastward orientation.
notes.14:19: The Hebrew term translated "Possessor" carries the dual sense of "Owner" and "Creator."
notes.14:22: Lifting up the hand to the LORD is a traditional Hebrew idiom for swearing a solemn oath.
notes.15:2: The Hebrew phrase rendered "heir of my household" uses a rare term that forms a wordplay with "Damascus."
notes.15:18: The Hebrew idiom for "made a covenant" literally means "cut a covenant," echoing the severed animal rite in verses 9-17.
notes.16:2: The Hebrew verb translated "be built up" plays on the word for "son," signifying establishing a family through offspring.
notes.16:5: The Masoretic Text marks the Hebrew word for "and you" with an extraordinary scribal dot above one of its letters.
notes.16:11: The name "Ishmael" means "God hears," matching the declaration that the LORD has heard Hagar's affliction.
notes.16:12: The Hebrew expression rendered "over against" can signify dwelling to the east of his kinsmen as well as living in hostility toward them.
notes.16:13: The Hebrew title "El Roi" means "God of seeing" or "God who sees me," and "Beer Lahai Roi" in verse 14 means "Well of the Living One who sees me."
notes.17:1: Hebrew El Shaddai, traditionally rendered God Almighty, emphasizes divine sufficiency and sovereign power in renewing the covenant.
notes.17:5: The name change from Abram, meaning exalted father, to Abraham echoes the Hebrew for father of a multitude, linking his new name to the promise of many nations.
notes.17:20: The clause "as for Ishmael, I have heard you" preserves a Hebrew wordplay on the name Ishmael, which means God hears.
notes.18:6: Literally "three seahs" of fine flour, a substantial dry measure amounting to roughly twenty quarts and signifying lavish hospitality.
notes.18:9: The Masoretic Text places extraordinary scribal dots above three letters of the Hebrew word for "to him," an ancient textual notation preserved in the manuscript tradition.
notes.18:10: The Hebrew idiom rendered "according to the time of life" refers to the return of this season in the coming year, matching the full course of childbirth.
notes.18:22: Classical Masoretic tradition lists this clause among the scribal adjustments (tiqqune sopherim), observing that "Abraham still stood before the LORD" expresses reverence rather than placing the LORD as standing before Abraham.
notes.19:11: The Hebrew term sanwerim denotes a sudden dazzling blindness or disorienting visual impairment, occurring elsewhere in the Old Testament only in 2 Kings 6:18.
notes.19:18: The Masoretic text points adonai here with a pausal long vowel; while contextually read as "my lords" addressing the angelic messengers (matching "to them"), some ancient traditions read it as "my Lord" addressing God directly.
notes.19:22: The name Zoar plays on the Hebrew word mitsar ("little one") used twice by Lot in verse 20.
notes.19:33: The Masoretic text marks the verb for "when she arose" with an extraordinary scribal dot (punctum extraordinarium); in verses 37-38, Moab echoes Hebrew for "from a father" and Ben-Ammi means "son of my people."
notes.20:13: The Hebrew verb "caused to wander" is grammatically plural with Elohim ("God"), a rare construction when referring to the one true God, possibly reflecting Abraham's manner of speaking before Abimelech.
notes.20:16: "A covering of the eyes" is a Hebrew idiom for a public compensatory gift that removes reproach and silences suspicion; the closing verb denotes being set right or publicly vindicated.
notes.20:18: The Hebrew uses an emphatic infinitive absolute construction (literally "closing, He had closed") to underscore that the LORD had completely shut every womb in Abimelech's household.
notes.21:6: Sarah's words play on the name Isaac, which derives from the Hebrew verb meaning to laugh.
notes.21:9: The Hebrew participle rendered "mocking" plays on Isaac's name and can denote scoffing, jesting, or playing.
notes.21:31: Beersheba means either "Well of the Oath" or "Well of Seven," uniting the seven ewe lambs and the oath sworn there in a single wordplay.
notes.21:33: "The Everlasting God" translates the Hebrew divine title El Olam, emphasizing God's eternal endurance and faithfulness.
notes.22:8: The Hebrew verb rendered "will provide" literally means "will see" or "will see to," anticipating the place name in verse 14.
notes.22:13: The Masoretic Hebrew reads "behind" rather than "one," though several ancient versions and manuscripts read "a" or "one" ram.
notes.22:14: "The LORD Will Provide" literally means "the LORD will see," and the passive verb at the end of the verse may mean either "it shall be provided" or "He shall be seen."
notes.22:18: The Hebrew Hithpael verb rendered "shall be blessed" can also be understood reflexively as "shall bless themselves."
notes.23:2: Kiriath Arba means "City of Arba," the earlier name of Hebron; the Masoretic Hebrew preserves the pentateuchal spelling of the feminine pronoun rendered "that is."
notes.23:6: Literally "a prince of God," a Hebrew idiom denoting greatness and dignity, equivalent to "a mighty prince."
notes.23:16: "Current among the merchants" refers to silver weighed out to recognized commercial standards in an era prior to minted coinage.
notes.23:17: Itemizing the trees within the boundaries reflects ancient Near Eastern property-transfer conventions ensuring complete conveyance of the land and all that stood on it.
notes.24:10: Aram Naharaim means Aram of the Two Rivers, denoting the region of northern Mesopotamia where Nahor's city of Haran lay.
notes.24:22: The weight of the nose ring is Hebrew beka, a half-shekel, and the bracelets are literally ten of gold, referring to ten shekels in weight.
notes.24:33: The translation follows the Masoretic Qere passive reading, food was set, where the consonantal Ketiv may reflect an older passive form or active he set.
notes.24:43: Hebrew almah denotes a young woman of marriageable age, varying the term from naarah, maiden, used earlier in the chapter.
notes.24:63: The Hebrew verb translated to meditate occurs only here in Scripture and has traditionally been understood as meditating or praying, though some take it to mean strolling through the field.
notes.25:18: Hebrew nafal literally means "he fell," used here idiomatically for settling or taking up one's allotted dwelling place opposite his kindred, echoing Genesis 16:12.
notes.25:23: The Masoretic text preserves a ketiv/qere orthographic variant (ketiv gyym, qere goyim), both meaning "nations"; the translation follows the qere.
notes.25:27: The Hebrew adjective tam describes Jacob as "complete," "mild," or "quiet," contrasting his domestic temperament with Esau's life in the open field.
notes.25:30: Esau's repeated call for "that red—that red stew" (Hebrew adom) creates a wordplay explaining his name Edom, while the verb rendered "let me eat" literally carries the coarse sense of gulping down food.
notes.26:4: The Hebrew Hithpael verb rendered "shall be blessed" can also carry a reflexive sense, "shall bless themselves," by invoking the blessing promised to Isaac's seed.
notes.26:8: The Hebrew verb translated "caressing" (metsacheq) forms a direct wordplay on the name Isaac (Yitschaq, "he laughs").
notes.26:19: "Living water" is the literal rendering of Hebrew mayim chayyim, denoting fresh, flowing spring water as distinct from standing cistern water.
notes.26:33: The name Shibah ("oath" or "seven") connects the well with the covenant oath just sworn between Isaac and Abimelech, explaining the name Beersheba ("well of the oath" or "well of seven").
notes.27:3: The Qere (read form) has the masculine noun for wild game, whereas the Ketiv (written form) carries an additional final letter often denoting provisions or game.
notes.27:29: The Qere (read form) reads the plural verb 'bow down' in agreement with 'nations,' whereas the Ketiv (written form) is written in the singular.
notes.27:36: Esau plays on the Hebrew name Jacob and the related verb meaning to supplant, deceive, or grasp by the heel.
notes.27:39: The Hebrew preposition rendered 'of' may also carry a privative sense, 'away from,' contrasting Esau's lot with Jacob's blessing in verse 28.
notes.28:12: The Hebrew term translated 'ladder' appears only here in the Old Testament and can also denote a stairway or stepped ramp.
notes.28:13: The Hebrew phrase rendered 'above it' (referring to the ladder) may alternatively be translated 'beside him' (referring to Jacob).
notes.28:19: The name Bethel means 'House of God,' echoing Jacob's exclamation in verse 17.
notes.29:1: "Lifted up his feet" is a literal Hebrew idiom conveying that Jacob set out briskly on his journey.
notes.29:17: The Hebrew adjective rendered "tender" can also mean "delicate" or "weak," contrasting with the description of Rachel's beauty.
notes.29:27: "The week of this one" refers to the customary seven-day bridal celebration for Leah before Rachel would also be given to Jacob.
notes.29:31: Literally "hated," a Hebrew idiom used in comparative family contexts to indicate being less favored or unloved.
notes.29:34: The Masoretic Hebrew reads an impersonal or masculine verb ("his name was called"), unlike the feminine forms in verses 32, 33, and 35. The names Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah each play in Hebrew on Leah's words ("looked," "heard," "joined," and "praise").
notes.30:8: The Hebrew expression translated 'fierce wrestlings' is literally 'wrestlings of God,' an idiom expressing great intensity.
notes.30:11: Following the Masoretic qere, 'Good fortune has come' (ba gad); the ketiv reads 'With good fortune' (begad).
notes.30:20: Leah's words play on the name Zebulun through two similar-sounding Hebrew roots meaning 'to endow' and 'to dwell with' (or 'to honor').
notes.30:27: The Hebrew verb rendered 'I have learned by divination' literally denotes observing or interpreting omens; Laban's opening 'If' clause breaks off in polite entreaty.
notes.31:19: Hebrew teraphim, rendered "household idols," refers to small domestic images tied to family religion and perhaps ancestral inheritance rights.
notes.31:20: Literally "stole the heart of Laban the Aramean" (see also verse 26), a Hebrew idiom for outwitting or deceiving someone by keeping them unaware.
notes.31:42: "The Fear of Isaac" (repeated in verse 53) is a reverent divine title designating God as the Awesome One whom Isaac revered and worshiped.
notes.31:47: Laban named the stone heap in Aramaic (Jegar Sahadutha) while Jacob named it in Hebrew (Galeed); both names mean "Heap of Witness."
notes.31:48: In this text, Laban's statement pointing to the heap and the pillar (numbered verse 51 in traditional versification) stands at the end of verse 48, so verse 50 is followed directly by verse 52.
notes.32:1: In the Masoretic Hebrew versification followed here, Genesis 32:1 corresponds to 31:55 in most English Bibles, shifting the verse numbering of chapter 32 forward by one.
notes.32:3: Mahanaim is a Hebrew dual form meaning Two Camps, reflecting both the camp of God's angels and Jacob's subsequent division of his own company into two camps.
notes.32:21: The Hebrew text weaves a fourfold play on the word panim, meaning face or presence, across this verse, foreshadowing Jacob's naming of Peniel, Face of God, in verse 31.
notes.32:33: The Hebrew phrase gid hannasheh denotes the sciatic sinew or tendon along the hip socket; note also the Hebrew spelling variation between Peniel in verse 31 and Penuel in verse 32.
notes.33:4: In the Masoretic Text, the Hebrew word for "and kissed him" bears extraordinary points above each letter, an ancient scribal marking traditionally prompting reflection on the emotion or sincerity of Esau's kiss.
notes.33:11: Jacob's expression "my blessing" echoes the blessing taken from Esau in Genesis 27, and his words "I have everything" contrast with Esau's "I have plenty" in verse 9.
